title.zh: 卷一百九十四 列傳第八十一: 忠義二
title.en: Volume 194 Biographies 81: Loyal and Righteous Acts 2
title.raw: 卷一百九十四 列傳第八十一: 忠義二 Volume 194 Biographies 81: Loyal and Righteous Acts 2

sentences.zh: 張桓，字彥威，真定藁城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Huan, style name Yanwei, was a man of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan, whose courtesy name was Yanwei, came from Gaocheng in Zhending Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父木，知汝寧府，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Mu was prefect of Runing Prefecture, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Mu had served as prefect of Runing, and the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 桓以國子生釋褐，授滑之白馬丞，入補中書掾，擢國子典簿。

translations.literal: Huan entered office as a Guozijian student, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Baima in Hua, supplemented as a Central Secretariat clerk, and was promoted to Imperial Academy registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Huan took office after graduating from the Imperial Academy, became assistant magistrate of Baima in Hua Prefecture, then filled a clerkship in the Central Secretariat and rose to registrar of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 拜陝西行台監察御史，以言事不合去。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and left because his remonstrances were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, but resigned when the court rejected his memorials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汝寧盜起，桓避之確山。

translations.literal: Before long bandits rose in Runing, and Huan fled to Queshan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rebels broke out in Runing, and Huan took refuge at Queshan.

sentences.zh: 賊久知桓名，襲獲之，羅拜請為帥，弗聽。

translations.literal: The bandits had long known Huan's name; they seized him in a raid, bowed in a circle, and asked him to be their leader, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long known his reputation; when they captured him in a surprise attack they bowed around him and begged him to lead them, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 囚六日，擁至渠魁前，桓直趨據榻坐，與之抗論逆順。

translations.literal: After six days in confinement they brought him before the ringleader; Huan went straight up, sat on the couch, and argued with him about loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Held for six days, he was dragged before the rebel chief; Huan walked straight to the couch, sat down, and debated with him the rights and wrongs of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其徒捽桓起跪，桓仰天大呼，詈叱彌厲，且屢唾賊面。

translations.literal: His men pulled Huan up and forced him to kneel; Huan looked to heaven and shouted, cursing all the more fiercely, and repeatedly spat in the bandits' faces.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him up and forced him to his knees, but he looked skyward and roared, cursing them ever more fiercely and spitting in their faces again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊猶不忍殺，謂桓曰：「汝但一揖，亦恕汝死。」

translations.literal: The bandits still could not bear to kill him and said to Huan, "If you will only bow once, we will spare your life."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still could not bring themselves to kill him and said, "Bow to us once and we will spare you."

sentences.zh: 桓瞋目曰：「吾恨不能手斬逆首，肯聽汝誘脅而折腰哉！」

translations.literal: Huan glared and said, "I regret that I cannot cut off the rebel leader's head with my own hand—how could I listen to your inducements and bend my waist!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan glared and cried, "I only regret that I cannot strike down the rebel chief with my own hand—do you think I would bend to your threats!"

sentences.zh: 賊知終不可屈，遂刺之。

translations.literal: When the bandits knew he could never be broken, they stabbed him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he would never yield, they stabbed him to death.

sentences.zh: 年四十八。

translations.literal: He was forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 賊後語人曰：「張御史真鐵漢，害之可惜！」

translations.literal: The bandits later said to people, "Supervisor Censor Zhang is a true man of iron—it was a pity to kill him!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels later told others, "Censor Zhang was a man of iron—it was a shame we had to kill him!"

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈禮部尚書，諡忠潔。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the court posthumously appointed him Minister of Rites and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Pure.

sentences.zh: 李黼，字子威，潁人也。

translations.literal: Li Fu, style name Ziwei, was a man of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, courtesy name Ziwei, was from Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書守中之子，守中性卞急，遇諸子極嚴，每一飲酒，輒半月醉不解，黼百計承順，求寧親心，終不可得，跪而自訟，往往達旦，無幾微厭怠之意。

translations.literal: He was the son of Minister of Works Li Shouzhong. Shouzhong was impetuous and stern toward his sons; whenever he drank he would remain drunk for half a month without sobering. Fu tried every means to please him and win his father's peace of mind but never succeeded; kneeling he would accuse himself, often until dawn, without the slightest sign of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Li Shouzhong, Minister of Works. Shouzhong was quick-tempered and harsh with his sons; each time he drank he stayed drunk for half a month. Fu tried every way to win his favor and calm him, but never could; he would kneel and reproach himself, often until dawn, without a trace of impatience.

sentences.zh: 初補國學生。

translations.literal: At first he was enrolled as an Imperial Academy student.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the Imperial Academy as a student.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，遂以明經魁多士，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he took first place among scholars in the Classics examination and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Taiding reign he topped the classics examination and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 明年，代祠西嶽，省臣謂黼曰：「敕使每後我，今可易邪？」

translations.literal: The next year, substituting in the sacrifice to the Western Peak, a provincial official said to Fu, "The imperial envoy always follows behind us—may we change that now?"
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while deputizing at the Western Peak sacrifice, a provincial minister asked Fu, "The imperial envoy always walks behind us—can we change the order this time?"

sentences.zh: 黼曰：「王人雖微，《春秋》序於諸侯之上，尊君也，奈何後乎！」

translations.literal: Fu said, "Though the king's envoy is low in rank, the Spring and Autumn Annals place him above the feudal lords—this honors the ruler; how can he come behind!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied, "However humble the king's envoy may be, the Spring and Autumn Annals rank him above the feudal lords—that is how one honors the sovereign. How could he walk behind us!"

sentences.zh: 省臣不敢對。

translations.literal: The provincial official did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial minister had no answer.

sentences.zh: 改河南行省檢校官，遷禮部主事，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of the Henan Branch Secretariat, promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites, and appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became an inspector in the Henan Branch Secretariat, then director in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 首言：「禴祠烝嘗，古今大祭，今太廟唯二祭，而日享佛祠、神御，非禮也，宜據經行之。

translations.literal: He first memorialized: "Yue, Zheng, and Chang are great sacrifices of ancient and modern times; today the Imperial Ancestral Temple has only two sacrifices, yet daily offers are made at Buddhist shrines and spirit tablets—this is not ritual; it should be carried out according to the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In his first memorial he wrote: "The seasonal sacrifices of spring, autumn, and winter are the great rites of every age, yet the ancestral temple now holds only two ceremonies while Buddhist shrines and spirit tablets are served daily—that is not proper ritual and should be brought back in line with the classics.

sentences.zh: 成均，教化之基，不當隸集賢，宜屬省臣兼領。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy is the foundation of education and should not be subordinate to the Academy of Gathered Talents; it should be jointly overseen by secretariat officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy is the foundation of education; it should not be placed under the Academy of Gathered Talents but overseen jointly by secretariat ministers.

sentences.zh: 諸侯王歲賜有定額，分封易代之際，陳請恩例，世系戚疏，無成書可考，宜仿先代，修正玉牒。」

translations.literal: Princes and kings have fixed annual grants; at times of enfeoffment and dynastic change they petition for favor, but lineage and kinship closeness have no authoritative record—one should follow earlier ages and revise the imperial genealogy."
translations.idiomatic: Princes receive fixed annual stipends, yet whenever titles are granted or dynasties change, petitions for favors pile up with no authoritative record of lineage and kinship—the court should follow earlier practice and revise the imperial genealogy."

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals received a reply.

sentences.zh: 轉江西行省郎中，入為國子監丞，遷宣文閣監書博士，兼經筵官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, entered service as Vice-Director of the Imperial Academy, and was promoted to Doctor of the Xuanwen Pavilion for Overseeing Books, concurrently serving on the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became a director in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, then vice-director of the Imperial Academy, and was promoted to doctor of the Xuanwen Pavilion in charge of books, also serving on the emperor's lecture staff.

sentences.zh: 數與勸講，每以聖賢心法為帝言之。

translations.literal: He often joined in exhorting the lectures and each time spoke to the emperor of the mind-methods of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently took part in the lecture sessions and always expounded to the emperor the inner teachings of the sages.

sentences.zh: 俄中書命黼巡視河渠，黼上言曰：「蔡河源出京西，宋以轉輸之故，平地作堤，今河底填淤，高出地面，秋霖一至，橫潰為災，宜按故跡修浚。

translations.literal: Soon the Central Secretariat ordered Fu to inspect rivers and canals. Fu memorialized: "The Cai River rises west of the capital; the Song, for transport, built dikes on level ground; now the riverbed is silted and stands above the ground—when autumn rains come it bursts sideways as a disaster; the old course should be dredged according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Central Secretariat sent him to inspect waterways. He memorialized: "The Cai River rises west of the capital. The Song built dikes on flat ground for grain transport, but the bed is now silted up above the surrounding land; when autumn rains come the river bursts and floods everywhere. The old channel should be dredged and restored.

sentences.zh: 他日東河或有不測之阻，江、淮運物，當由此分道達京，萬世之利也。」

translations.literal: If someday the eastern route should meet unforeseen obstruction, goods transported from the Yangzi and Huai could be sent by this route in branches to reach the capital—a benefit for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: If the eastern route were ever blocked, grain from the Yangzi and Huai could be sent along this line to the capital—a benefit for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: This too received no response.
translations.idiomatic: This proposal too went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 升秘書太監，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Supervisor of the Secretariat and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand supervisor of the Secretariat and appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 奉旨詳定中外所上封事。

translations.literal: By imperial order he reviewed and settled memorials submitted from within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he reviewed and adjudicated memorials submitted from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 已而廷議內外官通調，授黼江州路總管。

translations.literal: Before long the court discussed rotating officials internal and external, and Fu was appointed Prefect of Jiangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the court later decided on a general rotation of officials, Fu was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年夏五月，盜起河南，北據徐、蔡，南陷蘄、黃，焚掠數千里，造船北岸，銳意南攻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the eleventh year of Zhizheng, bandits rose in Henan, held Xu and Cai in the north, seized Qi and Huang in the south, burned and plundered for thousands of li, built boats on the north bank, and were keen to attack south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer in the eleventh year of Zhizheng, rebels broke out in Henan, seized Xu and Cai in the north and Qi and Huang in the south, burned and looted for thousands of li, built fleets on the north bank of the Yangzi, and pressed hard toward the south.

sentences.zh: 九江居下流，實江東、西襟喉之地，黼治城壕，修器械，募丁壯，分守要害，且上攻守之策於江西行省，請兵屯江北，以扼賊衝，庶幾大江之險，賊不得共之，不報。

translations.literal: Jiujiang lies on the lower reaches and is truly the throat of Jiangdong and Jiangxi; Fu repaired moats and walls, restored weapons, recruited strong youths, and divided forces to guard key points; he also submitted offensive and defensive plans to the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, asking troops to camp north of the river to block the bandits' thrust, so that perhaps with the Great River's barrier the bandits could not share it—but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang lay on the lower Yangzi, the strategic throat of the river lands east and west of it. Fu repaired walls and moats, restored arms, recruited able men, and posted guards at critical points; he also sent the Jiangxi authorities plans for attack and defense, asking that troops be stationed north of the river to block the rebel advance so they could not use the great river's barrier—but his plea went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 黼歎曰：「吾不知死所矣。」

translations.literal: Fu sighed and said, "I do not know where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Fu sighed, "I no longer know where I am to die."

sentences.zh: 乃獨椎牛饗士，激忠義以作士氣，數日之間，紀綱粗立。

translations.literal: He alone slaughtered an ox to feast the troops, roused loyalty and righteousness to lift morale, and within a few days discipline was roughly established.
translations.idiomatic: He alone slaughtered an ox to feast his men, stirred their loyalty and righteousness to raise morale, and within days had restored a measure of order.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月己未，賊渡江，陷武昌，威順王及省臣相繼遁，舳艫蔽江而下，江西大震。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei of the first month of the twelfth year the bandits crossed the river, took Wuchang, and the Weishun Prince and provincial officials fled one after another; boats and warships covered the river sailing down, and Jiangxi was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the first month of the twelfth year the rebels crossed the Yangzi and took Wuchang; the Prince of Weishun and the provincial officials fled in turn, and a fleet of warships filled the river sailing downstream—Jiangxi was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勝破瑞昌，右丞孛羅帖木兒方軍於江，聞之，遁。

translations.literal: The bandits followed their victory to break Ruichang; Right Chancellor Boluotiemuer was just encamped on the river, heard of it, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing their victory, the rebels took Ruichang. Right Chancellor Boluotiemuer, who had been encamped on the river, fled at the news.

sentences.zh: 黼雖孤立，辭氣愈奮厲。

translations.literal: Though Fu stood alone, his words and spirit grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Though he stood alone, Fu's words and bearing grew ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 時黃梅縣主簿也孫帖木兒，願出擊賊，黼大喜，向天瀝酒與之誓。

translations.literal: At the time Yesuntiemuer, chief clerk of Huangmei County, wished to go out and strike the bandits; Fu was greatly pleased and poured wine toward heaven to swear with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yesuntiemuer, chief clerk of Huangmei County, volunteered to lead a sortie; Fu was overjoyed and poured a libation to heaven to seal their oath.

sentences.zh: 言始脫口，賊遊兵已至境，急檄諸鄉落聚木石於險塞處，遏賊歸路。

translations.literal: The words had barely left his mouth when the bandits' scouting troops had already reached the border; he urgently ordered the villages to gather timber and stone at narrow passes to block the bandits' retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he spoken when rebel scouts were already at the border; he urgently ordered the countryside to pile timber and stone at narrow defiles to cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 倉卒無號，乃墨士卒面，統之出戰，黼身先士卒，大呼陷陣，也孫帖木兒繼進，賊大敗，逐北六十里。

translations.literal: In haste there were no unit marks, so he inked the soldiers' faces and led them out; Fu himself went before the troops, shouting as he broke the formation; Yesuntiemuer followed; the bandits were greatly defeated and pursued north sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: With no time to issue unit badges, he marked the soldiers' faces with ink and led them out. Fu charged at the head of the column, shouting as he broke the enemy line; Yesuntiemuer pressed behind; the rebels were routed and pursued sixty li.

sentences.zh: 鄉丁依險阻，乘高下木石，橫屍蔽路，殺獲二萬餘。

translations.literal: Village militia used the terrain, rolling timber and stone from heights; corpses blocked the road; more than twenty thousand were killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: Village militia used the high ground to roll down timber and stone; corpses choked the roads, and more than twenty thousand rebels were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 黼還，謂左右曰：「賊不利於陸，必由水道以舟薄我，苟失備禦，吾屬無唯類矣。」

translations.literal: When Fu returned he said to those around him, "The bandits are not suited to land—they must come by water with boats to press us; if we fail in defense, none of us will survive."
translations.idiomatic: On his return Fu told his staff, "The rebels fare poorly on land—they will surely come by water in boats to press us. If we fail to prepare, none of us will be left alive."

sentences.zh: 乃以長木數千，冒鐵椎於杪，暗植沿岸水中，逆刺賊舟，謂之七星樁。

translations.literal: He then took several thousand long timbers, capped their tips with iron spikes, and secretly planted them in the water along the shore to pierce bandit boats from below—calling them the Seven Stars Stakes.
translations.idiomatic: He drove thousands of long poles tipped with iron spikes into the riverbed along the shore to impale enemy boats from below—he called them the Seven Stars Stakes.

sentences.zh: 會西南風急，賊舟數千，果揚帆順流鼓譟而至，舟遇樁不得動，進退無措，黼帥將士奮擊，發火翎箭射之，焚溺死者無算，餘舟散走。

translations.literal: When a strong southwest wind arose, several thousand bandit boats indeed set sail downstream with drums and clamor; the boats struck the stakes and could not move, with no way to advance or retreat; Fu led the officers and soldiers in fierce attack, shooting fire-feathered arrows; countless were burned or drowned; the rest scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A strong southwest wind sprang up, and thousands of rebel boats sailed downstream with drums and shouts as expected. The boats struck the stakes and could neither advance nor retreat; Fu led his men in a fierce assault, shooting fire arrows; countless rebels were burned or drowned, and the rest scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 行省上黼功，請拜江西行省參政，行江州、南康等路軍民都總管，便宜行事。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat reported Fu's merit and requested appointment as Vice Administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, acting as Military-Civilian Commander-in-Chief of Jiangzhou, Nankang, and other circuits with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat reported his victories and asked that he be made vice administrator of Jiangxi, with overall military and civil command over Jiangzhou, Nankang, and neighboring circuits and discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 已而賊勢更熾，西自荊湖，東際淮甸，守臣往往棄城遁，黼守孤城，提孱旅，斬馘扶傷，無日不戰，中外援絕。

translations.literal: Before long the bandit power grew fiercer; from Jinghu in the west to the Huai region in the east, defending officials often abandoned cities and fled; Fu held a lone city, led a feeble force, cut heads and tended wounds, fought every day without pause, and aid from within and without was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels grew stronger still, from Jinghu in the west to the Huai plain in the east; defenders everywhere abandoned their cities and fled. Fu held a lone city with a weakened force, fighting daily, cutting down enemies and tending the wounded, while all aid from within and without was cut off.

sentences.zh: 二月甲申，賊將薄城，分省平章政事禿堅不花自北門遁。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the second month the bandits were about to press the city; the Branch Secretariat's Pacification Commissioner Tujianbuhua fled from the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the second month, as the rebels closed on the city, Pacification Commissioner Tujianbuhua of the branch secretariat fled through the north gate.

sentences.zh: 黼引兵登陴，布戰具，賊已至甘棠湖，焚西門，乃張弩箭射之。

translations.literal: Fu led troops onto the battlements, deployed war gear; the bandits had reached Gantang Lake, burned the west gate, and he drew crossbows and shot arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Fu led his men onto the walls and deployed weapons. The rebels had reached Gantang Lake and set fire to the west gate; he drew up crossbows and shot at them.

sentences.zh: 賊趑趄未敢進，轉攻東門。

translations.literal: The bandits hesitated and did not dare advance, then turned to attack the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hung back and did not dare advance, then turned to assault the east gate.

sentences.zh: 黼救東門，賊已入，與之巷戰，知力不敵，揮劍叱賊曰：「殺我！

translations.literal: Fu rushed to save the east gate, but the bandits had already entered; he fought them in the alleys; knowing his strength was insufficient, he waved his sword and shouted to the bandits, "Kill me!
translations.idiomatic: Fu raced to the east gate, but the rebels were already inside; he fought them street by street. Seeing he could not hold, he brandished his sword and shouted, "Kill me!

sentences.zh: 毋殺百姓！」

translations.literal: Do not kill the common people!"
translations.idiomatic: Spare the common people!"

sentences.zh: 賊自巷背來，刺黼墮馬，黼與從子秉昭俱罵賊而死。

translations.literal: Bandits came from behind in the alley, stabbed Fu and he fell from his horse; Fu and his nephew Bingzhao both cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came up from behind in the alley and stabbed him from his horse; Fu and his nephew Bingzhao cursed them as they died.

sentences.zh: 郡民聞黼死，器聲震天，相率具棺，葬於東門外。

translations.literal: When the people of the prefecture heard Fu had died, the sound of mourning shook heaven; they together prepared coffins and buried him outside the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard of his death, their wailing shook the heavens; they together prepared coffins and buried him outside the east gate.

sentences.zh: 黼死踰月，參政之命始下，年五十五。

translations.literal: More than a month after Fu's death the order for Vice Administrator arrived; he was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after his death the appointment as vice administrator finally arrived; he had been fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 黼兄冕居潁，亦死於賊。

translations.literal: Fu's elder brother Mian lived in Ying and also died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's elder brother Mian, who lived in Ying, also died at rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 秉昭，冕季子也。

translations.literal: Bingzhao was Mian's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhao was Mian's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈黼攄忠秉義效節功臣、資德大夫、淮南江北等處行中書省左丞、上護軍，追封隴西郡公，諡忠文。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Fu was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Subject Who Displays Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Dedicates His Life; Zide Grand Master; Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat for Huainan and Jiangbei; Upper Guardian General; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi; posthumous name Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the court posthumously granted Fu the title of meritorious subject who displayed loyalty and upheld righteousness, made him Zide Grand Master and left chancellor of the Huainan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat and upper guardian general, enfeoffed him posthumously as Duke of Longxi, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Literary.

sentences.zh: 詔立廟江州，賜額曰崇烈。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a temple established in Jiangzhou and granted the plaque name Chonglie (Revering Fierce Deeds).
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a temple built in Jiangzhou and bestowed the plaque title Revering Fierce Deeds.

sentences.zh: 官其子秉方集賢待制。

translations.literal: His son Bingfang was appointed Attendant Drafting Official of the Academy of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingfang was appointed attendant drafting official in the Academy of Gathered Talents.

sentences.zh: 李齊，字公平，廣平人。

translations.literal: Li Qi, style name Gongping, was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, courtesy name Gongping, was from Guangping.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧，客於江南，工辭章。

translations.literal: His family was very poor; he sojourned in Jiangnan and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: His family was very poor; he lived as a guest in the south and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 元統元年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he took first place among jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuantong reign he placed first in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷僉河南淮西廉訪司事，移知高郵府，有政聲。

translations.literal: He served as an official of the Henan-Huaixi Surveillance Commission, was transferred to be prefect of Gaoyou, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Henan-Huaixi surveillance commission, then became prefect of Gaoyou, where he earned a reputation for effective government.

sentences.zh: 至正十年，盜突入府驛，取十二馬去，齊躬追謝長等殺之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhizheng bandits suddenly entered the prefectural post station and took twelve horses; Qi personally pursued and killed Xie Chang and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhizheng, bandits raided the prefectural courier station and stole twelve horses; Qi pursued them in person and killed Xie Chang and his men.

sentences.zh: 十一年，州人秦觀保造兵仗，將圖劫掠，复獲而行誅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the man of the prefecture Qin Guanbao made weapons and planned to plunder; he was again captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a local man named Qin Guanbao forged weapons and plotted to raid the countryside; Qi captured him again and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，泰州白駒場亭民張士誠為亂，破泰州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhang Shicheng, a pavilion resident of Baiju Field in Taizhou, rebelled and broke Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhang Shicheng, a salt-worker of Baiju Field pavilion in Taizhou, rose in rebellion and overran Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 河南行省遣齊往招降，被拘。

translations.literal: The Henan Branch Secretariat sent Qi to summon surrender; he was detained.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Branch Secretariat sent Qi to negotiate their surrender, but he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 久之，賊酋自相殺，始縱齊來歸。

translations.literal: After a long time the bandit chiefs killed one another, and only then was Qi released to return.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the rebel chiefs turned on one another, and only then was Qi released to return.

sentences.zh: 泰州平，賊徒尚蜂聚，士誠复鼓變，殺參知政事趙璉，掠官庫民財，走入得勝湖，俄陷興化縣。

translations.literal: Taizhou was pacified, but bandit bands still swarmed; Shicheng again stirred rebellion, killed Vice Administrator Zhao Lian, plundered the government treasury and people's wealth, fled into Desheng Lake, and soon took Xinghua County.
translations.idiomatic: Though Taizhou was pacified, rebel bands still clustered together; Shicheng stirred up trouble again, killed Vice Administrator Zhao Lian, looted the government treasury and private wealth, fled into Desheng Lake, and soon overran Xinghua County.

sentences.zh: 行省以左丞偰哲篤偕宗王鎮高郵，使齊出守甓社湖。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat sent Left Chancellor Qiezhedu with a princely clan member to guard Gaoyou and had Qi go out to defend Bishe Lake.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat sent Left Chancellor Qiezhedu with a imperial clansman to hold Gaoyou and posted Qi to defend Bishe Lake.

sentences.zh: 夏五月乙未，數賊入城，一噪呼而省憲官皆遁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer on the day yiwei, several bandits entered the city; at one shout the provincial and surveillance officials all fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the fifth month of summer, a handful of rebels entered the city; at a single shout the provincial and surveillance officials all fled.

sentences.zh: 齊急還救城，賊已閉門拒我，遂連興化接得勝湖，舟艦四塞，蔓延入寶應縣。

translations.literal: Qi hurried back to save the city, but the bandits had already shut the gates to refuse them; they then linked Xinghua with Desheng Lake, boats and warships blocked on all sides, and spread into Baoying County.
translations.idiomatic: Qi rushed back to relieve the city, but the rebels had already shut the gates against him; they linked Xinghua with Desheng Lake, filled the waters with warships, and spread into Baoying County.

sentences.zh: 已而有詔：凡叛逆者赦之。

translations.literal: Before long there was an edict: all rebels were to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict arrived pardoning all rebels.

sentences.zh: 詔至高郵，不得入，賊紿曰：「請李知府來，乃受命。」

translations.literal: When the edict reached Gaoyou it could not enter; the bandits deceived them, saying, "Invite Prefect Li here, and then we will accept the order."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached Gaoyou the rebels would not let it in, claiming, "Send Prefect Li and we will accept the pardon."

sentences.zh: 行省強齊往，至則下齊獄中，齊益辯說，士誠本無降意，特遷延為繕飭計耳。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat forced Qi to go; when he arrived they put Qi in prison; Qi argued all the more; Shicheng had never intended to surrender—he only delayed as a plan to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat forced Qi to go; on arrival they threw him in prison. Qi argued ever more forcefully, but Shicheng had never meant to surrender—he was only stalling to regroup.

sentences.zh: 官軍諜知之，乃進攻城，士誠呼齊使跪，齊叱曰：「吾膝如鐵，豈肯為賊屈！」

translations.literal: Government troops learned this by espionage and advanced to attack the city; Shicheng called Qi to kneel; Qi shouted, "My knees are like iron—how could I bend to bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Government spies learned of this and advanced to besiege the city. Shicheng ordered Qi to kneel; Qi shouted, "My knees are iron—I will never bow to rebels!"

sentences.zh: 士誠怒，扼之跪，齊立而詬之，乃曳倒，搥碎其膝而呙之。

translations.literal: Shicheng was angry, forced him to kneel; Qi stood and cursed him; they dragged him down, smashed his knees with a mallet, and cut him apart.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng in rage forced him down, but Qi rose still cursing him; they dragged him down, smashed his knees with a mallet, and hacked him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 論者謂大科三魁，若泰不華沒海上，李黼隕九江，洎齊之死，皆不負所學云。

translations.literal: Commentators said that among the three top graduates of the great examination—Taibuhua perishing at sea, Li Fu falling at Jiujiang, and down to Qi's death—all did not betray what they had learned.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said that the three top graduates of the great examination—Taibuhua lost at sea, Li Fu fallen at Jiujiang, and now Qi at his death—none had betrayed what their learning had taught them.

sentences.zh: 褚不華，字君實，隰州石樓人，沉默有器局。

translations.literal: Chu Buhua, style name Junshi, was a man of Shilou in Xi Prefecture; he was reserved and had capacity and vision.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Buhua, courtesy name Junshi, came from Shilou in Xi Prefecture; he was quiet and possessed both talent and resolve.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，補中瑞司譯史，授海道副千戶，轉嘉興路治中，連拜南台、西台監察御史，遷河西道廉訪僉事，移淮東。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he was enrolled as a translator-clerk in the Zhongrui Office, appointed Deputy Commander of the Sea Route, transferred to Administrator of Jiaxing Circuit, successively appointed Supervising Censor of the Southern and Western Platforms, promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Hexi Circuit, and moved to Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign he entered service as a translator in the Zhongrui Office, became deputy commander of the sea route, then administrator of Jiaxing Circuit, and in succession supervising censor on the southern and western censorate platforms, surveillance commissioner on the Hexi circuit, and then Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，升副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 汝、潁盜發，勢張甚。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Ru and Ying; their power spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels broke out in the Ru and Ying region, and their power grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 不華行郡至淮安，極力為守禦計。

translations.literal: Buhua toured the prefecture to Huai'an and exerted himself fully in plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua toured the circuit as far as Huai'an and threw himself into plans for the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 賊至，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: When the bandits came, many were beheaded or captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, he killed or captured many of them.

sentences.zh: 且請知樞密院老章、判官劉甲守韓信城，相掎角為聲援。

translations.literal: He also asked that Laozhang of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Judge Liu Jia hold Hanxin City, supporting each other as mutual aid.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Laozhang of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Judge Liu Jia to hold Hanxin City so the two positions could support each other.

sentences.zh: 复上章，劾總兵及諸將逗撓之罪。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial impeaching the commander-in-chief and various generals for the crime of delay and shirking.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, impeaching the commander-in-chief and other generals for delay and shirking.

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄其功，升廉訪使，階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: The court recorded his merit and promoted him to Surveillance Commissioner, rank Zhongfeng Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The court recognized his achievements, promoted him to surveillance commissioner, and raised his rank to Zhongfeng Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 甲有智勇，與賊戰輒勝，賊憚之，號曰劉鐵頭，不華頗賴之。

translations.literal: Jia had wisdom and courage; whenever he fought bandits he won; the bandits feared him and called him Iron-Head Liu; Buhua relied on him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jia was resourceful and brave and won every engagement with the rebels, who feared him and called him Iron-Head Liu; Buhua relied heavily on him.

sentences.zh: 總兵者聞不華劾己，益恚嫉，乃檄甲別將兵擊賊，冀以困不華。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief heard Buhua had impeached him and grew all the more resentful; he then ordered Jia under a separate command to attack bandits, hoping thereby to distress Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief, hearing that Buhua had impeached him, grew more hostile and ordered Liu Jia away on a separate command against the rebels, hoping to weaken Buhua.

sentences.zh: 甲去，韓信城陷，賊乃掘塹相銜，揵水寨以圍我。

translations.literal: When Jia left, Hanxin City fell; the bandits then dug trenches linking one to another and drove water palisades to surround us.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jia departed, Hanxin City fell; the rebels dug linked trenches and built water palisades to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 既而天長青軍叛，普顏帖木爾所統黃軍复叛，賊皆挾之來攻​​不華知事危，退入哈剌章營。

translations.literal: Before long the Tianchang Green Army rebelled, and the Yellow Army under Puyantiemuer rebelled again; the bandits all brought them to attack. Buhua knew matters were critical and withdrew into the Halazhang camp.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tianchang Green Army mutinied, and the Yellow Army under Puyantiemuer rebelled as well; the rebels brought them all to the attack. Seeing the danger, Buhua withdrew into the Halazhang camp.

sentences.zh: 賊稍引去，乃出，抵楊村橋，賊奄至，殺廉訪副使不達失裡，啖其屍。

translations.literal: When the bandits slightly withdrew he came out, reached Yangcun Bridge; bandits suddenly arrived, killed Vice Surveillance Commissioner Budashili, and devoured his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels drew back slightly he came out and reached Yangcun Bridge, where they suddenly fell upon him, killed Vice Surveillance Commissioner Budashili, and devoured his body.

sentences.zh: 不華以餘兵入淮安。

translations.literal: Buhua entered Huai'an with the remaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua entered Huai'an with what troops remained.

sentences.zh: 時城之東、西、南三面皆賊，惟北門通沭陽，阻赤鯉湖，指揮使魏岳、楊暹駐兵沭陽，淮安倚其芻餉，而赤鯉湖為賊據，沭陽之路又絕。

translations.literal: At the time east, west, and south of the city were all bandits; only the north gate connected to Shuyang, blocked by Chili Lake; Commanders Wei Yue and Yang Xian stationed troops at Shuyang; Huai'an relied on their fodder and grain, but Chiyu Lake was held by bandits and the Shuyang road was again cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels now held the east, west, and south of the city; only the north gate led toward Shuyang across Chiyu Lake, where Commanders Wei Yue and Yang Xian were encamped. Huai'an depended on them for fodder and grain, but the rebels now held Chiyu Lake and the route to Shuyang was cut.

sentences.zh: 賊計孤城可取，進柵南瑣橋。

translations.literal: The bandits judged the lone city could be taken and advanced palisades to Nan Suo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels judged the isolated city could be taken and advanced their palisades to Nan Suo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 不華與元帥張存義出大西門，會僉事忽都不花兵突賊柵，殊死戰，賊敗走，追北二十餘里。

translations.literal: Buhua and Marshal Zhang Cunyi went out the great west gate, joined Commissioner Hudubuhua's troops in a sudden strike on the bandit palisades, fought a desperate battle, the bandits were defeated and fled, and they pursued north more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua and Marshal Zhang Cunyi sallied from the great west gate, joined Commissioner Hudubuhua's troops in a sudden assault on the rebel palisades, fought a desperate battle, routed the rebels, and pursued them more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 城中食且絕，元帥吳德琇運糧萬斛入河，竟為賊所掠，德琇僅以身免。

translations.literal: Food in the city was nearly exhausted; Marshal Wu Dexiu transported ten thousand hu of grain into the river, but it was finally plundered by bandits; Dexiu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Food in the city was nearly gone. Marshal Wu Dexiu tried to bring ten thousand hu of grain up the river, but the rebels seized it all; Dexiu barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 賊與青軍攻圍，日益急，總兵者屯下邳，相去五百里，按兵不出，凡遣使十九輩告急，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Bandits and the Green Army pressed the siege ever more urgently; the commander-in-chief was encamped at Xiapi, five hundred li away, held his troops and did not advance; nineteen messengers were sent in all to report urgency, but none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels and the Green Army tightened the siege day by day. The commander-in-chief sat at Xiapi five hundred li away and would not move; nineteen urgent messengers were sent, and none was heeded.

sentences.zh: 城中餓者僕道上，即取噉之，一切草木、螺蛤、魚蛙、燕烏，及靴皮、鞍韂、革箱、敗弓之筋皆盡，而後父子夫婦老稚更相食，撤屋為薪，人多露處，坊陌生荊棘。

translations.literal: The starving in the city fell in the streets and were taken and eaten; all plants, snails, clams, fish, frogs, swallows, and crows, as well as boot leather, saddle pads, leather boxes, and sinews from broken bows were exhausted; then fathers and sons, husbands and wives, old and young ate one another; houses were torn down for fuel; most people slept in the open; lanes and markets grew thorny weeds.
translations.idiomatic: The starving collapsed in the streets and were eaten on the spot; every plant, shellfish, fish, frog, bird, boot leather, saddle pad, leather box, and bowstring was consumed; then families turned on one another; houses were torn down for firewood; most slept in the open, and thorns overran the lanes.

sentences.zh: 力既盡，城陷，不華猶據西門力鬥，中傷見執，為賊所臠。

translations.literal: When strength was exhausted the city fell; Buhua still held the west gate and fought fiercely; wounded, he was captured and dismembered by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When their strength was spent the city fell. Buhua still held the west gate and fought on until he was wounded, captured, and cut to pieces by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 次子伴哥，冒刃護之，亦見殺。

translations.literal: His second son Bange, braving blades to protect him, was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Bange rushed through the blades to shield him and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 時至正十六年十月乙丑也。

translations.literal: This was on the day yichou of the tenth month of the sixteenth year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the yichou day of the tenth month of the sixteenth year of Zhizheng.

sentences.zh: 不華守淮安五年，殆數十百戰，精忠大節，人比之張巡云。

translations.literal: Buhua defended Huai'an for five years, fighting perhaps scores or hundreds of battles; his pure loyalty and great integrity led people to compare him to Zhang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua had defended Huai'an for five years through scores of battles; for his pure loyalty and steadfast integrity people compared him to Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，贈翰林學士承旨、榮祿大夫、柱國，追封衛國公，諡曰忠肅，賻鈔二百錠，以卹其家。

translations.literal: When the court heard, it posthumously granted him Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin, Ronglu Grand Master, and Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Weiguo; posthumous name Zhongsu; bestowed two hundred ingots of paper money to comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, it posthumously made him Hanlin expositor-in-chief, Ronglu Grand Master, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed him as Duke of Weiguo with the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn, and granted two hundred ingots of paper money to support his family.

sentences.zh: 郭嘉，字元禮，濮陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Jia, style name Yuanli, was a man of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia, courtesy name Yuanli, was from Puyang.

sentences.zh: 祖昂，父惠，俱以戰功顯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ang and father Hui both became prominent through military merit.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ang and father Hui had both won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 嘉慷慨有大志，始由國子生登泰定三年進士第，授彰德路林州判官，累遷翰林國史院編修官，除廣東道宣慰使司都元帥府經歷。

translations.literal: Jia was magnanimous with great ambition; he first entered office as a Guozijian student and passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taiding; was appointed Assistant Prefect of Linzhou in Zhangde Circuit; was repeatedly promoted to Compiler in the Hanlin National History Institute; and was appointed Administrator of the Guangdong Pacification Commissioner's Grand Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was generous and ambitious. He entered office through the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taiding, became assistant prefect of Linzhou in Zhangde Circuit, rose to compiler in the Hanlin National History Institute, and was made administrator of the Guangdong pacification commissioner's grand marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為京畿漕運使司副使，尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Before long he entered service as Vice Commissioner of the Capital Region Grain Transport Office, and soon was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became vice commissioner of the capital region grain transport office, and soon was appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以海寇起，欲於浙東溫、台、慶元等路立水軍萬戶鎮之，眾論紛紜莫定。

translations.literal: When sea bandits arose the court wished to establish naval commanders of ten thousand households in Wen, Tai, Qingyuan, and other circuits of eastern Zhe to guard against them; public opinion was divided and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When sea raiders appeared, the court proposed establishing naval commanders of ten thousand households in Wen, Tai, Qingyuan, and other eastern Zhe circuits, but opinion was divided and no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 擢嘉禮部員外郎，乘驛至慶元，與江浙行省會議可否。

translations.literal: Jia was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, traveled by courier post to Qingyuan, and conferred with the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat on whether it was feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Rites, traveled by courier to Qingyuan, and met with the Jiang-Zhe authorities to decide the matter.

sentences.zh: 嘉至，首詢父老，知其弗便，請罷之。

translations.literal: When Jia arrived he first questioned the elders and learned it was inconvenient; he requested it be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he first consulted local elders, learned the plan would be burdensome, and asked that it be dropped.

sentences.zh: 會方擇守令綏靖遼東，乃授嘉廣寧路總管，兼諸奧魯勸農防禦。

translations.literal: As they were selecting prefects and magistrates to pacify Liaodong, Jia was appointed Prefect of Guangning Circuit, concurrently Overseer of Agriculture and Defense for all Oru.
translations.idiomatic: As the court was choosing officials to pacify Liaodong, Jia was appointed prefect of Guangning Circuit, with concurrent charge of agriculture and defense for the Oru communities.

sentences.zh: 屬盜起，軍旅數興，供餉無虛日。

translations.literal: Bandits arose in the region; armies were repeatedly raised; supplies were needed every day without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels broke out in the region, troops were raised again and again, and supplies were demanded without a day's respite.

sentences.zh: 民苦和糴轉輸，而吏胥得因時為奸。

translations.literal: The people suffered from government purchase and transport levies, while clerks and runners took advantage of the times to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned under government grain purchases and transport levies while clerks exploited the crisis for their own gain.

sentences.zh: 嘉設法計其戶口，第其甲乙，民甚便之。

translations.literal: Jia devised a method to tally households and rank them in grades A and B; the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jia devised a system to register households and rank them by grade, which greatly eased the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 有詔團結義兵，嘉招集民數千，教以坐作進退，萬、千、百夫各統以長，號令齊一，賞罰明信。

translations.literal: An edict ordered rallying righteous militia; Jia gathered several thousand civilians, taught them drill in sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating; commanders of ten thousand, thousand, and hundred each led them; orders were uniform; rewards and punishments were clear and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the rallying of loyal militia, Jia gathered several thousand men, drilled them in formation, organized them under commanders of ten thousand, thousand, and hundred, and enforced uniform orders with clear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 故東方諸郡，錢糧之富，甲兵之精，稱嘉為最。

translations.literal: Therefore among the eastern prefectures, in wealth of money and grain and excellence of armor and troops, Jia was said to be foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among the eastern circuits he was reckoned foremost in wealth of revenue and quality of arms and troops.

sentences.zh: 十八年，寇陷上京，嘉聞之，躬率義兵出禦。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year invaders took Shangjing; when Jia heard he personally led righteous militia out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the rebels took Shangjing; on hearing the news Jia personally led his militia out to resist them.

sentences.zh: 既而遼陽陷，嘉將眾巡邏，去城十五里，遇青號隊伍百餘人，始言官軍，嘉疑其詐，俄果脫青衣變紅。

translations.literal: Before long Liaoyang fell; Jia led troops on patrol fifteen li from the city, met a band of more than a hundred in green insignia who at first claimed to be government troops; Jia suspected deception, and soon they indeed stripped green garments and changed to red.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liaoyang fell. Jia was patrolling fifteen li from the city when he met a band of more than a hundred men in green who claimed to be government troops; suspecting a ruse, he watched as they stripped off their green coats and donned red rebel colors.

sentences.zh: 嘉出馬射賊，分兵兩隊而夾攻之，生擒賊數百，死者無算。

translations.literal: Jia rode out and shot at bandits, divided troops into two columns to attack from both sides, captured several hundred bandits alive, and killed countless others.
translations.idiomatic: Jia rode out and shot at them, split his force into two columns to attack from both flanks, took several hundred prisoners, and killed countless others.

sentences.zh: 嘉見賊勢日熾，孤城無援，乃集同官議攻守之計，眾皆失措，嘉曰：「吾計決矣。」

translations.literal: Jia saw bandit power growing daily and the lone city without aid; he gathered fellow officials to discuss plans for attack and defense; all were at a loss; Jia said, "My plan is settled."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rebel strength grow daily and his isolated city without aid, Jia gathered his colleagues to discuss defense; all were at a loss until he said, "My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 因竭家所有衣服財物犒義士，以勵其勇敢，且曰： 「自我祖宗，有勳王室，今之盡忠，吾分內事也。

translations.literal: He then exhausted all his family's clothing and goods to reward the righteous warriors and encourage their bravery, saying, "From my ancestors onward we have had merit for the royal house; to be loyal now is my proper duty.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all his family's clothing and goods to reward the militia and stir their courage, saying, "My ancestors have served the throne with merit; to be loyal now is simply my duty.

sentences.zh: 況身守此土，當生死以之，餘不足卹矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, guarding this land in person, I should live and die with it; the rest is not worth grieving."
translations.idiomatic: As the one charged to hold this land, I owe it my life; nothing else matters."

sentences.zh: 頃之，賊至，圍城亙數十里，有大呼者曰：「遼陽我得矣，何不出降！」

translations.literal: Before long bandits arrived and besieged the city for several tens of li; someone shouted loudly, "I have taken Liaoyang—why do you not surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels came and encircled the city for miles. Someone shouted, "Liaoyang is mine—why don't you surrender!"

sentences.zh: 嘉挽弓射呼者，中其左頰，墮馬死，賊稍引退，嘉遂開西門逐之，賊大至，力戰以死。

translations.literal: Jia drew his bow and shot the shouter, hitting his left cheek; he fell from his horse and died; the bandits slightly withdrew; Jia then opened the west gate and pursued; bandits came in force and he fought fiercely until death.
translations.idiomatic: Jia drew his bow and shot the shouter through the left cheek; the man fell dead from his horse and the rebels drew back slightly. Jia opened the west gate in pursuit, but when the main rebel force arrived he fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈崇化宣力效忠功臣、資善大夫、河南江北等處行省左丞、上護軍，封太原郡公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted Meritorious Subject Who Promotes Transformation, Displays Power, and Dedicates Loyalty; Zishan Grand Master; Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat for Henan and Jiangbei; Upper Guardian General; enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan; posthumous name Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the court posthumously granted him the title of meritorious subject who promoted transformation and displayed loyal service, made him Zishan Grand Master and left chancellor of the Henan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat and upper guardian general, enfeoffed him as Duke of Taiyuan, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 喜同，周姓，河西人。

translations.literal: Xitong, surname Zhou, was a man of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Xitong, of the Zhou clan, came from Hexi.

sentences.zh: 初為后宮衛士，眾稱其才，選充承徽寺經歷，再調南陽縣達魯花赤。

translations.literal: At first he was a guard of the inner palace; all praised his talent; he was selected as Administrator of the Chenghui Temple, then transferred to be Darughachi of Nanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a guard in the inner palace, where his ability won praise; he was made administrator of the Chenghui Temple, then transferred to be darughachi of Nanyang County.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，妖賊起，陷鄧州，人情洶洶。

translations.literal: After two years demonic bandits rose and took Dengzhou; popular sentiment was turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: After two years rebel bands rose and took Dengzhou, and panic spread through the region.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊鋒抵南陽，南陽無城無兵，賊入之若虛邑。

translations.literal: Before long the bandit vanguard reached Nanyang; Nanyang had no walls and no troops; bandits entered as if it were an empty town.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebel vanguard reached Nanyang, which had neither walls nor troops; the rebels entered as if it were an empty town.

sentences.zh: 喜同以計獲數賊，詰之，雲賊將大至。

translations.literal: Xitong by stratagem captured several bandits and questioned them; they said a great bandit force was coming.
translations.idiomatic: Xitong captured several rebels by stratagem and questioned them; they said a large force was on its way.

sentences.zh: 悉斬之，以安眾心，晝夜督丁壯巡邏守備。

translations.literal: He beheaded them all to calm popular hearts and day and night supervised strong youths in patrol and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He executed them all to steady the people's nerves and day and night pressed the able-bodied men into patrol and defense.

sentences.zh: 時大司農錢木爾，以兵駐於諸葛庵，為賊所襲，死之。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Minister of Agriculture Qian Mu'er was encamped with troops at Zhuge Hermitage and was attacked by bandits and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Qian Mu'er was then encamped with troops at Zhuge Hermitage; the rebels attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賊遂乘銳取南陽。

translations.literal: The bandits then seized their momentum to take Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then pressed their advantage and took Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 喜同守西門，望見賊勢盛，即以死自許，與家人訣曰：「吾與汝等不能相顧矣，但各逃生，吾分死此，以報國也。」

translations.literal: Xitong guarded the west gate; seeing the bandit force was strong he pledged himself to death and took leave of his family, saying, "You and I cannot look after one another—each escape as you can; my portion is to die here and repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: Xitong held the west gate; seeing the rebel force was overwhelming, he resolved to die and bade his family farewell: "We cannot look after one another—each of you escape as you can. My part is to die here and repay the state."

sentences.zh: 已而城中皆哭，喜同策厲義兵，奮力與賊搏，賊退去。

translations.literal: Before long the whole city was weeping; Xitong spurred the righteous militia and fought the bandits with all his strength; the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the whole city was weeping. Xitong rallied the militia and fought the rebels with all his strength, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日復至，與戰甚力，殺賊凡數百。

translations.literal: The next day they came again; he fought very fiercely and killed several hundred bandits in all.
translations.idiomatic: They returned the next day; he fought fiercely again and killed several hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊知無後援，戰愈急，南陽遂陷。

translations.literal: The bandits knew there was no rear support and fought ever more urgently; Nanyang then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had no reinforcements, the rebels pressed harder and Nanyang fell.

sentences.zh: 喜同突圍將自拔，賊橫刺其馬，馬蹶，喜同鞭馬躍而起，手斬刺馬者。

translations.literal: Xitong broke out of the encirclement and was about to escape; bandits stabbed his horse crosswise; the horse fell; Xitong whipped the horse and leaped up, personally beheading the one who stabbed the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Xitong broke through the encirclement and was about to escape when a rebel stabbed his horse; as the horse fell Xitong lashed it, leaped up, and cut down the man who had stabbed it.

sentences.zh: 俄而為他賊所追，身被數創，不能鬥，遂見執，為所殺。

translations.literal: Before long other bandits pursued him; his body received many wounds; he could not fight; he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels soon overtook him; wounded many times, he could fight no longer, was captured, and killed.

sentences.zh: 妻邢氏，聞喜​​同力戰死，帥家僮數人出走，遇賊，奪賊刀斫之，且罵且前，亦見殺。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Xing, hearing Xitong had died fighting fiercely, led several household servants in flight; they met bandits; she seized a bandit's knife and hacked at them, cursing as she advanced, and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Xing, hearing he had died fighting, fled with several servants; meeting rebels she seized one's knife, hacked at them, cursing as she advanced, and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 一家死者二十餘人。

translations.literal: More than twenty of the household died.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty members of the household died.

sentences.zh: 贈南陽路判官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Judge of Nanyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed judge of Nanyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 韓因，字可宗，汴梁人。

translations.literal: Han Yin, style name Kezong, was a man of Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yin, courtesy name Kezong, was from Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 少習舉子業，負氣不群。

translations.literal: In youth he studied examination arts and was proud-spirited, not mixing with others.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied for the civil examinations and was proud and solitary by nature.

sentences.zh: 盜據汝寧，官軍討之，久不下。

translations.literal: Bandits held Runing; government troops attacked but could not take it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Runing, and government troops besieged it for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷詔赦叛逆，募可持詔入賊者，即藉以官。

translations.literal: When the court issued an edict pardoning rebels and recruited one who could carry the edict into the bandits, he would be granted office on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued an edict pardoning rebels and sought someone who could carry it into the rebel camp, promising an official post in return.

sentences.zh: 因應命，乃借因以唐州判官，使焉。

translations.literal: Yin answered the call; they lent Yin the title of Assistant Prefect of Tangzhou and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin volunteered; they lent him the title of assistant prefect of Tangzhou and sent him on the mission.

sentences.zh: 賊渠恐其黨心搖，導因止於外，納詔不讀，詰問再三，因答以「恩宥寬大，禍福所繫」，甚切。

translations.literal: The bandit chief feared his followers' hearts would waver, guided Yin to stop outside, received the edict but did not read it, questioned him repeatedly; Yin answered that "the grace of pardon is broad, fortune and misfortune hang upon this," very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief, fearing his men might waver, kept Yin outside, took the edict but would not read it, and questioned him repeatedly. Yin urged that "the pardon is generous and your fate hangs upon this" with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 不聽，乃縱因歸報。

translations.literal: They did not listen and released Yin to return with a report.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen and let Yin return to report.

sentences.zh: 因出，乘馬周賊屯，大言曰：「汝輩好百姓，何不出降歸田裡，而甘從逆賊驅使耶！」

translations.literal: Yin went out, rode his horse around the bandit encampments, and shouted loudly, "You are good common people—why do you not surrender and return to your fields, but willingly follow rebel bandits' commands!"
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, Yin rode around the rebel camps shouting, "You are honest folk—why not surrender and return to your fields instead of serving rebels!"

sentences.zh: 眾愕眙相顧。

translations.literal: The crowd stared in astonishment at one another.
translations.idiomatic: The men stared at one another in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 或以告賊渠，渠追因，責其所言。

translations.literal: Someone reported to the bandit chief; the chief pursued Yin and reproached him for his words.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this to the rebel chief, who pursued Yin and rebuked him for his words.

sentences.zh: 因極口肆詈，賊怒，寸割因。

translations.literal: Yin cursed with all his mouth; the bandits were angry and dismembered Yin inch by inch.
translations.idiomatic: Yin cursed them with all his might; the rebels in rage cut him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 卞琛，大名人。

translations.literal: Bian Chen, a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Chen was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 世為農夫，早遊學京師，得補國子生，既而丁母憂，治農於家。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers; he early traveled to study in the capital, was enrolled as a Guozijian student, then entered mourning for his mother and managed farming at home.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations; he studied in the capital in his youth and entered the Imperial Academy, then after his mother's death returned home to farm.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，鄰郡盜起。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng bandits rose in a neighboring prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng rebels broke out in a neighboring prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，來剽掠，琛與從子小十、府史李仲亨等協謀，統丁壯數百人擊賊。

translations.literal: Before long they came to plunder; Chen with his nephew Xiaoshi, prefectural clerk Li Zhongheng, and others plotted together and led several hundred strong youths to attack bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they came raiding; Chen with his nephew Xiaoshi, prefectural clerk Li Zhongheng, and others joined in a plan and led several hundred able men against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 丁壯皆民兵，無弓矢之備，直以鉤鋤白鋌當賊。

translations.literal: The strong youths were all militia without bows and arrows; they faced bandits directly with hooks, hoes, and plain spears.
translations.idiomatic: The militia had no bows or arrows and faced the rebels with nothing but hooks, hoes, and spears.

sentences.zh: 賊矢雨集，琛眾潰散，被擒。

translations.literal: Bandit arrows fell like rain; Chen's force scattered in defeat and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel arrows fell like rain; Chen's force broke and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 仲亨、小十皆死。

translations.literal: Zhongheng and Xiaoshi both died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongheng and Xiaoshi both died.

sentences.zh: 賊素知琛，諭之曰：「汝從我，解汝縛；

translations.literal: The bandits had long known Chen and admonished him, saying, "If you follow me, I will release your bonds;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, who knew Chen well, urged him: "Join us and we will free you;

sentences.zh: 不從，殺汝。」

translations.literal: if you do not follow, I will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: refuse and we will kill you."

sentences.zh: 琛唾罵曰：「我國子生也。

translations.literal: Chen spat and cursed, saying, "I am a Guozijian student.
translations.idiomatic: Chen spat and cursed: "I am an Imperial Academy student.

sentences.zh: 視汝逆賊，真狗彘也。

translations.literal: Looking at you rebel bandits, you are truly dogs and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: You rebels are nothing but dogs and swine.

sentences.zh: 吾寧義死，不從賊生！」

translations.literal: I would rather die for righteousness than live following bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die honorably than live as a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 罵不止。

translations.literal: He did not stop cursing.
translations.idiomatic: He would not stop cursing.

sentences.zh: 賊屢脅不聽，殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits repeatedly threatened him but he would not listen; they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threatened him again and again, but he would not yield, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 喬彝，字仲常，晉寧人。

translations.literal: Qiao Yi, style name Zhongchang, was a man of Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yi, courtesy name Zhongchang, was from Jinning.

sentences.zh: 性高介有守，一時名稱籍甚。

translations.literal: His nature was lofty and principled; his reputation at the time was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He was proud and principled by nature, and his reputation at the time was very great.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，賊由絳州垣曲縣襲晉寧。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng bandits from Yuanqu County in Jiang Prefecture attacked Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng rebels from Yuanqu County in Jiang Prefecture raided Jinning.

sentences.zh: 城陷，城中死者十二三。

translations.literal: The city fell; one or two tenths of those in the city died.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell, and ten or twenty percent of its people were killed.

sentences.zh: 彝整冠衣，聚妻子，家有大井，彝坐井上，令妻子婢輩循次投井中，而己隨赴之。

translations.literal: Yi arranged cap and robes, gathered wife and children; the family had a great well; Yi sat on the well and ordered wife, children, and maidservants in turn to cast themselves into the well, then he followed after them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi put on his cap and robes, gathered his wife and children; the family had a great well. Yi sat on its rim and ordered his wife, children, and servants to throw themselves in one by one, then followed them in.

sentences.zh: 彝既死，賊首王士誠使人即彝家邀致之，至則彝已死矣。

translations.literal: After Yi had died, the bandit chief Zhang Shicheng sent men immediately to Yi's home to invite him; when they arrived Yi was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, the rebel chief Zhang Shicheng sent men to fetch him to his home, but when they arrived Yi was already dead.

sentences.zh: 賊平，朝廷贈彝臨汾縣尹，賜諡純潔。

translations.literal: When bandits were pacified the court posthumously granted Yi Magistrate of Linfen County and bestowed the posthumous name Chunjie.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, the court posthumously appointed Yi magistrate of Linfen County and gave him the posthumous title Pure and Upright.

sentences.zh: 有張岩起、王佐者，皆士人也，並以不屈賊而死。

translations.literal: There were Zhang Yanqi and Wang Zuo, both scholars, who both died for refusing to yield to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanqi and Wang Zuo were also scholars who died rather than submit to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 岩起字傅霖，汾州人。

translations.literal: Yanqi, style name Fulin, was a man of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi, courtesy name Fulin, was from Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累舉不中，嘗用薦者徵為國子助教。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented himself for examination without success; once through recommendation he was summoned as Assistant Instructor of the Guozijian.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the examinations repeatedly, but was once summoned through recommendation as assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 居一歲，免歸。

translations.literal: After one year he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 盜既去晉寧，复陷汾州，岩起與妻赴井​​死。

translations.literal: After bandits left Jinning they again took Fen Prefecture; Yanqi and his wife cast themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels left Jinning they took Fen Prefecture; Yanqi and his wife threw themselves into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 王佐字元輔，晉寧人。

translations.literal: Wang Zuo, style name Yuanfu, was a man of Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuo, courtesy name Yuanfu, was from Jinning.

sentences.zh: 從父居上都，教授里巷，不與時俯仰。

translations.literal: He followed his father to live at Shangdu, teaching in the lanes, not bending with the times.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed his father to Shangdu, where he taught in the neighborhoods and would not bend with the times.

sentences.zh: 會賊至，倉卒不能避，為所獲，欲降之。

translations.literal: When bandits came he could not avoid them in haste; he was seized; they wished him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came he could not escape in time; they captured him and tried to make him surrender.

sentences.zh: 佐傲岸自如，詬賊不輟，因見害。

translations.literal: Zuo remained proud and aloof as before, cursing bandits without cease, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo remained proud and unbowed, cursing the rebels without cease, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 又有吳德新者，字止善，建昌人。

translations.literal: There was also Wu Dexin, style name Zhishan, a man of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wu Dexin, courtesy name Zhishan, from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 工醫，留京師，久之，嘗往寧夏。

translations.literal: Skilled in medicine, he stayed in the capital; after a long time he once went to Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled physician, he had long stayed in the capital and once traveled to Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 會盜至，德新見執，脅使降，德新厲聲曰：「我生為皇元人，死作皇元鬼，誓不從爾賊！」

translations.literal: When bandits came Dexin was seized and compelled to surrender; Dexin said in a stern voice, "Living I am a man of the Great Yuan; dead I shall be a ghost of the Great Yuan—I swear I will not follow you bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came he was seized and ordered to surrender. Dexin cried in a fierce voice, "Born a subject of the Great Yuan, I shall die a ghost of the Great Yuan—I will never follow you rebels!"

sentences.zh: 賊乃縛其兩手，加白刃頸上，迫其畏屈，德新罵不已。

translations.literal: The bandits bound both his hands and placed a bare blade on his neck to force him to fear and bend; Dexin did not stop cursing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound his hands and laid a blade to his neck to frighten him into submission, but Dexin would not stop cursing.

sentences.zh: 乃曳之井上，陽欲擠之。

translations.literal: They then dragged him to a well and pretended they would push him in.
translations.idiomatic: They dragged him to a well and pretended they would push him in.

sentences.zh: 德新偶得寬，即自投井中，仰罵賊。

translations.literal: Dexin chanced to gain slack and immediately cast himself into the well, looking up and cursing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Finding a moment's slack, Dexin at once threw himself into the well and cursed the rebels from below.

sentences.zh: 賊下射，矢貫其頂，罵益力。

translations.literal: Bandits shot down; an arrow pierced his crown; he cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shot down at him; an arrow pierced his crown, yet he cursed all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，以長槍刺之。

translations.literal: The bandits were angry and stabbed him with a long spear.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels stabbed him with a long spear.

sentences.zh: 然亦壯其志，憐其死，曰：「此真丈夫也！」

translations.literal: Yet they also admired his resolve and pitied his death, saying, "This is a true man!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet they admired his spirit and pitied his death, saying, "This was a true man!"

sentences.zh: 以土埋井而去。

translations.literal: They buried the well with earth and left.
translations.idiomatic: They filled the well with earth and departed.

sentences.zh: 顏瑜，字德潤，兗州曲阜人，兗國复聖公五十七代孫也。

translations.literal: Yan Yu, style name Derun, was a man of Qufu in Yan Prefecture, fifty-seventh-generation descendant of the Duke of Fusheng of the State of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yu, courtesy name Derun, was from Qufu in Yan Prefecture, the fifty-seventh-generation descendant of the Duke of Fusheng.

sentences.zh: 以行誼用舉者，為鄒及陽曲兩縣教諭。

translations.literal: Recommended for his conduct and friendship, he was Instructor of both Zou and Yangqu counties.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for his character and conduct, he served as instructor in both Zou and Yangqu counties.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，田豐起山東，瑜攜家走鄆城，道遇賊，以刃來脅瑜曰：「爾何人？」

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng Tian Feng rose in Shandong; Yu took his family and fled toward Yuncheng; on the road he met bandits who came with blades to threaten Yu, saying, "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, Tian Feng rebelled in Shandong. Yu fled with his family toward Yuncheng and met rebels on the road who threatened him with blades, demanding, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 瑜曰：「我東魯書生也。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "I am a scholar of eastern Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "I am a scholar from eastern Lu."

sentences.zh: 賊執瑜曰： 「爾書生，吾不爾殺，可從我見主帥。」

translations.literal: The bandits seized Yu and said, "You are a scholar—I will not kill you; you may come with me to see the commander."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized him and said, "You are a scholar—we will not kill you. Come with us to see our commander."

sentences.zh: 瑜罵曰：「爾賊，何主帥邪！」

translations.literal: Yu cursed, "You bandits—what commander!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu cursed them: "You rebels—what commander!"

sentences.zh: 賊怒，欲殺瑜，瑜無懼色。

translations.literal: The bandits were angry and wished to kill Yu, but Yu showed no fear.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in anger meant to kill him, but Yu showed no fear.

sentences.zh: 復使之寫旗，瑜大詬曰：「爾大元百姓，天下亂，募爾為兵，而反為叛逆。

translations.literal: They again made him write a banner; Yu cursed loudly, "You are subjects of the Great Yuan; the realm is in turmoil and you were recruited as soldiers, yet you turn rebel.
translations.idiomatic: They again ordered him to write a rebel banner. Yu cursed loudly: "You are subjects of the Great Yuan. The realm is in chaos and you were recruited as soldiers—yet you rebel!

sentences.zh: 我腕可斷，豈能為爾寫旗從逆乎！」

translations.literal: My wrist may be cut off—how could I write banners for you and follow rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: You may cut off my wrist—I will never write your banners and join your rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 賊以槍刺瑜，至死罵不絕口。

translations.literal: The bandits stabbed Yu with a spear; until death he did not stop cursing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stabbed him with a spear; he cursed without cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 其妻子皆為所害。

translations.literal: His wife and children were all killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were all killed as well.

sentences.zh: 又有曹彥可者，亳州人。

translations.literal: There was also Cao Yanke, a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cao Yanke, from Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 會妖寇起里中，多田野無賴子，目不知書者。

translations.literal: When demonic bandits rose in the village, most were idle fellows of the fields who could not recognize written characters.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel bands rose in the countryside, most were idle ruffians from the fields who could not read.

sentences.zh: 既破亳，揭帛於竿，皆群趨彥可家劫之，使寫旗。

translations.literal: After they took Bo, they hung silk on poles; all rushed in a crowd to Yanke's home to rob him and make him write banners.
translations.idiomatic: After they took Bo, they raised banners on poles and swarmed to Yanke's home to seize him and make him write rebel standards.

sentences.zh: 彥可力辭，乃迫以刀斧。

translations.literal: Yanke strenuously refused; they then compelled him with blades and axes.
translations.idiomatic: Yanke refused firmly, so they threatened him with blades and axes.

sentences.zh: 彥可唾之曰：「我儒者，知有君父，寧死耳，豈為汝寫旗者耶！」

translations.literal: Yanke spat at them and said, "I am a Confucian who knows there are ruler and father; I would rather die—how could I be one who writes banners for you!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanke spat at them: "I am a Confucian who knows ruler and father. I would rather die than write your banners!"

sentences.zh: 賊怒，遂見害，年七十矣。

translations.literal: The bandits were angry and killed him; he was seventy.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in anger killed him. He was seventy years old.

sentences.zh: 其家素貧，又死於亂，藁殯其屍。

translations.literal: His family had always been poor; he also died in the turmoil; his corpse was buried in straw.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor; he died in the chaos, and his body was buried in a straw coffin.

sentences.zh: 賊既定，有司具以事聞，中書為給貲以葬，賜諡節愍。

translations.literal: When bandits were pacified the authorities reported the affair in full; the Central Secretariat provided funds for burial and bestowed the posthumous name Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, officials reported the affair; the Central Secretariat provided funds for burial and granted the posthumous title Steadfast and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 王士元，字堯佐，恩州人。

translations.literal: Wang Shiyuan, style name Yaozuo, was a man of En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyuan, courtesy name Yaozuo, was from En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年進士，由棣州判官累遷知磁州。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Taiding, from Assistant Prefect of Di Prefecture he was repeatedly promoted to Magistrate of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourth year of Taiding, he rose from assistant prefect of Di Prefecture to magistrate of Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 值軍興，饋餉需索日繁，民不堪命。

translations.literal: When military campaigns arose, supply demands grew daily; the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out, supply demands multiplied daily and the people could not endure the burden.

sentences.zh: 士元心念其民，力為區畫，至為將士陵辱訶責，弗避也。

translations.literal: Shiyuan kept the people in mind and strove to plan for them, even suffering insult and reproach from officers and soldiers without avoiding it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan kept his people in mind and worked hard to ease their burdens, even when officers insulted and rebuked him for it.

sentences.zh: 改知浚州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Magistrate of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州濱黃河，嘗經盜賊，城堞不完，市井空荒，士元邑邑不得志，而臨事未嘗易其素。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered the Yellow River, had often suffered bandits, walls were incomplete, markets empty and desolate; Shiyuan was depressed and unfulfilled, yet in facing affairs he never changed his principles.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay on the Yellow River, had often been ravaged by bandits, its walls were broken and its markets deserted. Shiyuan was deeply frustrated, yet he never compromised his principles in office.

sentences.zh: 至正十七年，賊复迫浚州，州兵悉潰散，士元坐堂上，顧其子致微使避賊，曰：「吾守臣，居此，職也。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhizheng bandits again pressed Jun Prefecture; prefectural troops all scattered in defeat; Shiyuan sat in the hall, looked at his son Zhiwei and told him to avoid the bandits, saying, "I am a defending official—staying here is my duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhizheng rebels again pressed Jun Prefecture; the garrison scattered in defeat. Shiyuan sat in the hall, told his son Zhiwei to flee the rebels, and said, "I am the defending official—staying here is my duty.

sentences.zh: 若可逃生。」

translations.literal: You may escape with your life."
translations.idiomatic: You should save yourself."

sentences.zh: 子侍立，不忍去。

translations.literal: His son stood attending and could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: His son stood by his side and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 賊前問曰：「爾為誰？」

translations.literal: The bandits came forward and asked, "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came forward and asked, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 士元叱曰：「我王知州也。

translations.literal: Shiyuan shouted, "I am Prefect Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan shouted, "I am Prefect Wang!

sentences.zh: 強賊識我否？」

translations.literal: Do you violent bandits know me?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you brutes know who I am?"

sentences.zh: 賊欲縛士元，士元奮拳毆賊，賊怒，併其子殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to bind Shiyuan; Shiyuan struck bandits with his fists; the bandits were angry and killed him together with his son.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to bind him; Shiyuan struck out with his fists. Enraged, they killed him and his son together.

sentences.zh: 楊朴，字文素，河南人。

translations.literal: Yang Pu, style name Wensu, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu, courtesy name Wensu, was from Henan.

sentences.zh: 早以文學得推擇為吏，任至滁州全椒縣尹。

translations.literal: Early through literary learning he was selected and promoted as an official, serving up to Magistrate of Quanjiao County in Chuzhou.
