translations.idiomatic: Early on his literary talent won him office, and he rose to magistrate of Quanjiao County in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 滁界廬江，廬江陷於寇，滁人震動。

translations.literal: Chuzhou bordered Lujiang; Lujiang fell to raiders; the people of Chuzhou were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou bordered Lujiang, which had fallen to raiders, and the people of Chuzhou were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 行省參政也先總兵於滁，不理軍事，唯縱飲，至暮，城門不鑰，寇入縱火，猶張燭揮杯，急逾城出走。

translations.literal: Branch Secretariat Vice Administrator Yexian commanded troops at Chuzhou, paid no attention to military affairs, only indulged in drink; by evening the city gates were not locked; raiders entered and set fires; he still spread candles and waved cups, then urgently fled over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Yexian of the branch secretariat commanded troops at Chuzhou but ignored military affairs and drank freely. By evening the gates were unlocked; raiders entered and set fires while he still feasted by candlelight, then fled over the wall in haste.

sentences.zh: 樸度必死，乃盡殺其妻女，朝服坐堂上。

translations.literal: Pu judged he must die, so he killed all his wife and daughters, put on court robes, and sat in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Pu knew he must die, killed his wife and daughters, donned his court robes, and sat in the hall.

sentences.zh: 盜欲降之，樸指妻女示曰：「我已戕我屬，政欲死官守耳，尚何云雲！」

translations.literal: Bandits wished him to surrender; Pu pointed to his wife and daughters and showed them, saying, "I have already killed my household—I only wish to die holding office; what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tried to make him surrender. Pu pointed to his dead wife and daughters and said, "I have already killed my family—I mean only to die at my post. What more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 乃連唾之。

translations.literal: He then spat at them repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He spat at them again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊縶樸，倒懸樹上，而割其肉至盡，猶大罵弗絕。

translations.literal: Bandits bound Pu, hung him upside down on a tree, and cut his flesh until none remained; he still cursed loudly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound him, hung him upside down from a tree, and cut his flesh away piece by piece; he still cursed without cease.

sentences.zh: 趙璉，字伯器，宏偉之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhao Lian, style name Boqi, was the grandson of Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lian, courtesy name Boqi, was the grandson of Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，登進士第，授嵩州判官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhizhi reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant prefect of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再調汴梁路祥符縣尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be Magistrate of Xiangfu County in Bianliang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Xiangfu County in Bianliang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為國子助教。

translations.literal: He entered service as Assistant Instructor of the Guozijian.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷湖廣行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Left and Right Offices of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the left and right offices of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 除杭州路總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Hangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Hangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 杭於東南為劇郡，地大民夥，長吏多不稱其職。

translations.literal: Hangzhou in the southeast was a demanding prefecture, vast in territory with a large population; senior officials often did not fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou was one of the most demanding prefectures in the southeast, vast and populous, and its senior officials often failed in their duties.

sentences.zh: 璉為人強毅開敏，精力絕人，吏莫不服其明決，而不敢欺。

translations.literal: Lian was strong, resolute, and quick-witted, with energy surpassing others; clerks all submitted to his clarity and decisiveness and did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was forceful, resolute, and quick-witted, with tireless energy; his clerks respected his clarity and decisiveness and dared not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 浙右病於徭役，民充坊里正者，皆破其家。

translations.literal: Zheyou suffered from corvée labor; commoners who served as ward and village heads all ruined their families.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhe suffered under corvée burdens; those who served as ward and village heads often ruined their families.

sentences.zh: 朝廷令行省召八郡守集議便民之法，璉獻議以屬縣坊正為僱役，里正用田賦以均之，民咸以為便。

translations.literal: The court ordered the Branch Secretariat to summon prefects of eight prefectures to discuss methods benefiting the people; Lian submitted a proposal that subordinate county ward heads be hired labor, village heads use land tax to equalize burdens—the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the branch secretariat to gather eight prefects to discuss reforms. Lian proposed hiring ward heads as paid labor and funding village heads from land tax assessments; the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 有盜誘其同惡，持刃出市，斫人以索金，市民乃戶斂以予之，人無敢言者。

translations.literal: A thief induced his accomplices, took blades into the market, hacked people to extort gold; townspeople then collected household by household to give to them, and no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: A thief recruited accomplices who took blades into the market and hacked people to extort money; the townspeople paid household by household, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 璉曰：「此不可長也。」

translations.literal: Lian said, "This cannot be allowed to continue."
translations.idiomatic: Lian said, "This cannot be tolerated."

sentences.zh: 遣卒掩捕之，盡戮諸市。

translations.literal: He sent soldiers to seize them in a surprise raid and executed them all in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He sent soldiers to seize them in a surprise raid and executed them all in the market.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was summoned to the capital as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 杭人思之，刻其政績於碑。

translations.literal: The people of Hangzhou missed him and carved his achievements on a stele.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Hangzhou missed him and carved his achievements on a stele.

sentences.zh: 歷中書左司郎中，除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He served as Director in the Central Secretariat Left Office and was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Central Secretariat's left office and was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 尋遷戶部，拜參議中書省事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and appointed Councilor of Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he moved to the Ministry of Revenue and was appointed councilor of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為山北遼東道廉訪使。

translations.literal: He went out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Shanbei-Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei-Liaodong circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時河南兵起，湖廣、荊襄皆陷，而兩淮亦騷動。

translations.literal: At this time armies rose in Henan; Huguang and Jingxiang all fell, and the two Huai regions were also in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Armies had risen in Henan; Huguang and Jingxiang had fallen, and the two Huai regions were in turmoil as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃析河南地，立淮南江北行省於揚州，以璉參知政事。

translations.literal: The court then divided Henan territory and established the Huainan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat at Yangzhou, appointing Lian Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The court then carved out territory from Henan, established the Huainan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat at Yangzhou, and made Lian vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 璉方病水腫，即輿疾而行。

translations.literal: Lian was then ill with edema but immediately traveled by litter despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was suffering from edema but set out at once by litter.

sentences.zh: 既至，分省鎮淮安，又移鎮真州。

translations.literal: After arriving, the Branch Secretariat garrisoned Huai'an, then moved the garrison to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival the branch secretariat stationed at Huai'an, then moved its headquarters to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會張士誠為亂，突起海濱，陷泰州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shicheng rebelled, he suddenly rose on the seacoast and took Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng rebelled, rising suddenly on the coast and taking Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 興化，行省遣兵討之，不克。

translations.literal: and Xinghua; the Branch Secretariat sent troops to attack but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Xinghua, but troops sent by the branch secretariat could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 乃命高郵知府李齊往招諭之。

translations.literal: They then ordered Gaoyou Prefect Li Qi to go and summon him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They then ordered Gaoyou Prefect Li Qi to go and negotiate his surrender.

sentences.zh: 士誠因請降，行省授以民職，且乞從征討以自效。

translations.literal: Shicheng thereupon requested surrender; the Branch Secretariat granted him a civilian post and he also begged to follow campaigns to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng then offered to surrender; the branch secretariat gave him a civilian post and he asked to join campaigns to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遂移璉鎮泰州，璉乃趣士誠治戈船，趨濠、泗。

translations.literal: Lian was then moved to garrison Taizhou; Lian urged Shicheng to prepare weapons and boats and advance toward Hao and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was moved to garrison Taizhou and urged Shicheng to ready arms and boats for an advance on Hao and Si.

sentences.zh: 士誠疑憚不肯發，又覘知璉無備，遂復反。

translations.literal: Shicheng hesitated and feared and would not set out; he also spied and learned Lian was unprepared, then rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng hesitated and refused to march; learning that Lian was unprepared, he rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓，縱火登城。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night he set fires and scaled the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch of the night he set fires and stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 璉力疾捫佩刀上馬，與賊鬥市衢。

translations.literal: Lian, forcing himself despite illness, felt for his belt knife, mounted a horse, and fought bandits in the market streets.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his illness Lian seized his belt knife, mounted, and fought the rebels in the market streets.

sentences.zh: 賊圍璉，邀至其船，璉詰之曰：「汝輩罪在不赦，今既宥爾誅戮，又錫以名爵，朝廷何負于汝，乃既降復反邪！

translations.literal: Bandits surrounded Lian and invited him to their boat; Lian reproached them, saying, "Your crimes are unpardonable; now that your executions have been pardoned and titles and ranks bestowed, what has the court done against you, that you surrender and rebel again!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels surrounded him and invited him aboard their boat. Lian rebuked them: "Your crimes deserve death. The court pardoned you and granted you titles—what wrong did it do you, that you surrender and rebel again!

sentences.zh: 汝棄信逆天，滅不旋踵。

translations.literal: You abandon faith and oppose Heaven—you will perish in no time.
translations.idiomatic: You abandon faith and defy Heaven—you will perish in no time.

sentences.zh: 我執政大臣，豈為汝賊輩屈乎！」

translations.literal: I am a chief minister of state—how could I bow to you bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: I am a chief minister of state—do you think I would bow to rebels like you!"

sentences.zh: 即馳騎奮擊賊，賊以槊撞璉墜地，欲舁登其舟，璉瞋目大罵，遂死之。

translations.literal: He immediately spurred his horse and fiercely struck bandits; bandits knocked Lian from his horse with a spear-shaft, wished to lift him onto their boat; Lian glared and cursed loudly, and they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse and charged at them. The rebels knocked him from his horse with a spear and tried to drag him aboard, but Lian glared and cursed them fiercely until they killed him.

sentences.zh: 其僕揚兒以身蔽璉，亦俱死。

translations.literal: His servant Yang'er shielded Lian with his body and also died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Yang'er shielded him with his body and died with him.

sentences.zh: 及亂定，州民收其屍，歸殯於真州。

translations.literal: When the turmoil was settled the people of the prefecture collected his corpse and returned it for burial at Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored the people collected his body and buried it at Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賻鈔三百錠，仍官其子錡。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, three hundred ingots of paper money were granted as condolence payment, and his son Qi was given office.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the court granted three hundred ingots of paper money as condolence and appointed his son Qi to office.

sentences.zh: 弟琬，字仲德，仕至台州路總管。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wan, style name Zhongde, served up to Prefect of Taizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wan, courtesy name Zhongde, rose to prefect of Taizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至正二十七年，方國瑛以舟挾琬至黃岩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhizheng Fang Guoying took Wan by boat to Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhizheng, Fang Guoying took Wan by boat to Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 琬潛登白龍奧，舍於民家，絕粒不食。

translations.literal: Wan secretly climbed to Bailong Ao, lodged in a commoner's home, and ceased eating grain entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Wan secretly went up to Bailong Ao, lodged with a common family, and stopped eating altogether.

sentences.zh: 人勸之食，輒瞑目卻之，七日而死。

translations.literal: When people urged him to eat he would close his eyes and refuse; after seven days he died.
translations.idiomatic: When people urged him to eat he closed his eyes and refused; after seven days he died.

sentences.zh: 孫捴，字自謙，曹州人。

translations.literal: Sun Cuan, style name Ziqian, was a man of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cuan, courtesy name Ziqian, was from Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至正二年進士，授濟寧路錄事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Zhizheng, he was appointed Recorder of Jining Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the second year of Zhizheng, he was appointed recorder of Jining Circuit.

sentences.zh: 張士誠據高郵叛，或謂其有降意，朝廷擇烏馬兒為使，招諭士誠，而用捴輔行。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou in rebellion; some said he had intent to surrender; the court chose Wuma'er as envoy to summon Shicheng, using Cuan as assistant on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou in rebellion, some thought he might surrender. The court chose Wuma'er as envoy to negotiate with him and appointed Cuan as his assistant.

sentences.zh: 捴家居，不知也。

translations.literal: Cuan was at home and did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan was at home and knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 中書借捴集賢待制，給驛，就其家起之。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat borrowed Cuan as Attendant Drafting Official of the Academy of Gathered Talents, provided courier post, and raised him from his home.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat appointed him attendant drafting official in the Academy of Gathered Talents, sent a courier, and summoned him from his home.

sentences.zh: 捴強行抵高郵，士誠不迓詔使。

translations.literal: Cuan forced his way to Gaoyou; Shicheng did not welcome the imperial envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan pressed on to Gaoyou, but Shicheng did not welcome the imperial envoy.

sentences.zh: 捴等既入城，反覆開諭，士誠等皆竦然以聽。

translations.literal: After Cuan and others entered the city they repeatedly exhorted and instructed; Shicheng and others all listened with startled attention.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the city they exhorted him repeatedly, and Shicheng and his men listened with apparent attention.

sentences.zh: 已而拘之他室，或日一饋食，或間日一饋食，欲以降捴，捴唯詬斥而已。

translations.literal: Before long they detained him in another room, sometimes feeding him once a day, sometimes once every other day, wishing to make Cuan surrender; Cuan only cursed and reproached.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they confined him elsewhere, feeding him once a day or every other day, hoping to make him submit; Cuan only cursed them.

sentences.zh: 乃令其黨捶捴，肆其陵辱，捴不恤也。

translations.literal: They then ordered his followers to beat Cuan and indulge in insult; Cuan paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: They had their men beat and humiliate him, but Cuan paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 及士誠徙平江，捴與士誠部將張茂先謀，將捴所授站馬劄子，遣壯士浦四、許誠赴鎮南王府，約日進兵復高郵。

translations.literal: When Shicheng moved to Pingjiang, Cuan plotted with Shicheng's officer Zhang Maoxian, taking the courier-horse warrant Cuan had been given, and sent stalwarts Pu Si and Xu Cheng to the Prince of Zhennan's mansion to arrange a date for advancing troops to recover Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shicheng moved to Pingjiang, Cuan plotted with his officer Zhang Maoxian, using the courier warrant he had been given to send stalwarts Pu Si and Xu Cheng to the Prince of Zhennan's mansion to arrange a date for retaking Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 謀洩，執捴訊問，捴罵聲不絕，竟為所害。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; they seized Cuan for interrogation; Cuan's curses did not cease; in the end he was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; they seized Cuan for questioning, but he cursed without cease and was killed.

sentences.zh: 後賊中見失節者，輒自相嗤曰：「此豈孫待制耶！」

translations.literal: Later among bandits when they saw one who lost integrity they would mock one another, saying, "Is this Attendant Drafting Official Sun!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when rebels saw someone who had lost his integrity, they would mock one another: "Is this Attendant Drafting Official Sun!"

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈翰林侍讀學士、中奉大夫、護軍，追封曹南郡公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted Hanlin Attendant Reader, Zhongfeng Grand Master, and Guardian General; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Caonan; posthumous name Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the court posthumously made him Hanlin attendant reader, Zhongfeng Grand Master, and guardian general, enfeoffed him as Duke of Caonan, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 賜田三頃卹其家。

translations.literal: Three qing of land were granted to comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: Three qing of land were granted to support his family.

sentences.zh: 石普，字元周，徐州人。

translations.literal: Shi Pu, style name Yuanzhou, was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu, courtesy name Yuanzhou, was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 至正五年進士，授國史院編修官，改經正監經歷。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifth year of Zhizheng, he was appointed Compiler of the National History Institute, then transferred to Administrator of the Jingzheng Office.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fifth year of Zhizheng, he was appointed compiler in the National History Institute, then administrator of the Jingzheng Office.

sentences.zh: 淮東、西盜起，朝廷方用兵，普以將略稱，同僉樞密院事董鑰嘗薦其材，會丞相脫脫討徐州，以普從行。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in eastern and western Huai; the court was then deploying troops; Pu was famed for military strategy; Associate Censor-in-Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs Dong Yue once recommended his talent; when Chancellor Toghto attacked Xuzhou, Pu accompanied the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose in eastern and western Huai while the court was at war. Pu was known for military talent; Dong Yue of the Bureau of Military Affairs had recommended him, and when Chancellor Toghto attacked Xuzhou, Pu joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 徐平錄功，遷兵部主事，尋升樞密院都事，從樞密院官守淮安。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified his merit was recorded; he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of War, soon elevated to Chief Clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and followed Bureau officials to guard Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuzhou was pacified his merit was recorded; he became director in the Ministry of War, then chief clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and followed bureau officials to guard Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 時張士誠據高郵，普詣丞相，面陳破賊之策，且曰：「高郵負重湖之險，地皆沮洳，騎兵卒莫能前，與普步兵三萬，保取之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou; Pu went to the Chancellor and stated in person a plan to break the bandits, saying, "Gaoyou relies on the barrier of heavy lakes; the ground is all marsh; cavalry and infantry at last cannot advance—give Pu thirty thousand foot soldiers and I guarantee taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng then held Gaoyou. Pu went to the chancellor and presented a plan in person: "Gaoyou is protected by great lakes and marshland where cavalry cannot pass. Give me thirty thousand foot soldiers and I guarantee its capture.

sentences.zh: 高郵既平，則濠、泗易破，普請先驅，為天下忠義倡。」

translations.literal: Once Gaoyou is pacified, then Hao and Si are easily broken; Pu requests to lead the vanguard and be a champion of loyalty and righteousness for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaoyou falls, Hao and Si will be easy to take. I ask to lead the vanguard and set an example of loyalty for the realm."

sentences.zh: 丞相壯之，命權山東義兵萬戶府事，招民義萬人以行。

translations.literal: The Chancellor was impressed and ordered him to act as Commander of the Shandong Righteous Militia Ten-Thousand-Household Office, recruiting ten thousand civilian volunteers to march.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor was impressed and appointed him acting commander of the Shandong righteous militia office, recruiting ten thousand volunteers for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 而汝中柏者方用事，陰沮之，減其軍半。

translations.literal: But Bo Zhe of Runing was then in power and secretly obstructed him, reducing his army by half.
translations.idiomatic: But Bo Zhe of Runing was then in power and secretly obstructed him, cutting his force in half.

sentences.zh: 初令普便宜行事，及行，又使聽淮南行省節制。

translations.literal: At first Pu was ordered to act at discretion; when he marched, he was again made to obey the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At first Pu was authorized to act at discretion; when he marched he was again placed under the Huainan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 普行次範水寨，日未夕，普令軍中具食，夜漏三刻，下令銜枚趨寶應，其營中更鼓如平時。

translations.literal: Pu halted at Fanshui Stockade; the sun had not yet set when Pu ordered the army to prepare food; at the third watch of the night he ordered troops to take twigs in their mouths and hurry to Baoying; in the camp the watch-drums sounded as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Pu halted at Fanshui Stockade. Before sunset he ordered the army to prepare food; at the third watch he ordered silent advance on Baoying while the camp drums sounded as on an ordinary night.

sentences.zh: 抵縣，即登城，樹幟城上，賊大驚潰，因撫安其民。

translations.literal: Reaching the county he immediately mounted the walls, raised banners atop the city, bandits were greatly startled and fled, and he thereby pacified the people.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the county he scaled the walls at once and raised his banners; the rebels fled in panic, and he pacified the people.

sentences.zh: 由是諸將疾普功，水陸進兵，乘勝拔十餘寨，斬賊數百。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals resented Pu's merit; they advanced by land and water, following victory to take more than ten stockades and behead several hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals resented his success; advancing by land and water they followed up with more than ten stockades taken and several hundred rebels killed.

sentences.zh: 將抵高郵城，分兵三隊：一趨城東，備水戰；

translations.literal: About to reach Gaoyou city, he divided troops into three columns: one toward the east of the city to prepare for naval combat;
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Gaoyou, he divided his force into three columns: one toward the east of the city for naval combat;

sentences.zh: 一為奪兵，虞後；

translations.literal: one as a striking force to guard the rear;
translations.idiomatic: one as a reserve to guard the rear;

sentences.zh: 一普自將，攻北門。

translations.literal: one led by Pu himself to attack the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: and one under Pu himself to assault the north gate.

sentences.zh: 遇賊與戰，賊不能支，遁入城。

translations.literal: They met bandits and fought; bandits could not hold and fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: They met the rebels in battle; unable to hold, the rebels fled into the city.

sentences.zh: 普先士卒躡之，縱火燒關門，賊懼，謀棄城走。

translations.literal: Pu went before the troops in pursuit, set fire and burned the gate tower; bandits were afraid and plotted to abandon the city and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Pu charged at the head of his men, set fire to the gate tower; the rebels in fear planned to abandon the city and flee.

sentences.zh: 而援軍望之，按不進。

translations.literal: But the relief army saw this and held their troops without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: But the relief army looked on and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 且忌普成功，總兵者遣蒙古軍千騎，突出普軍前，欲收先入之功。

translations.literal: Moreover they envied Pu's success; the commander-in-chief sent a thousand Mongol cavalry who burst out before Pu's army, wishing to seize the merit of entering first.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous of his success, the commander-in-chief sent a thousand Mongol cavalry to rush ahead of Pu's army and claim the credit for entering first.

sentences.zh: 而賊以死捍，蒙古軍恇怯，即馳回，普止之不可，遂為賊所蹂踐，率墜水中。

translations.literal: But bandits defended to the death; Mongol troops were timid and cowardly and immediately galloped back; Pu could not stop them; they were then trampled by bandits and mostly fell into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels defended to the death; the Mongol troops panicked and galloped back. Pu could not stop them; they were trampled by the rebels and most fell into the water.

sentences.zh: 普軍亂，賊乘之。

translations.literal: Pu's army was in disorder and bandits seized the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's army fell into disorder and the rebels pressed their advantage.

sentences.zh: 普勒餘兵，血戰良久，仗劍大呼曰：「大丈夫當為國死，有不進前者，斬！」

translations.literal: Pu rallied the remaining troops and fought a bloody battle for a long time; holding his sword he shouted loudly, "A great man should die for the state—whoever does not advance, behead!"
translations.idiomatic: Pu rallied what troops remained and fought a bloody battle for a long time, sword in hand shouting, "A true man dies for his country—whoever does not advance will be cut down!"

sentences.zh: 奮擊，直入賊陣中，從者僅三十人。

translations.literal: He struck fiercely and charged straight into the bandit formation; followers were only thirty men.
translations.idiomatic: He charged straight into the rebel ranks with only thirty men following.

sentences.zh: 至日西，援絕，被創墮馬，复步戰數合。

translations.literal: When the sun went west aid was cut off; wounded he fell from his horse, then fought on foot for several rounds.
translations.idiomatic: By sunset reinforcements were cut off; wounded, he fell from his horse and fought on foot for several more rounds.

sentences.zh: 賊益至，賊指曰：「此必頭目，不可使逸，須生致之。」

translations.literal: Bandits came in greater numbers; bandits pointed and said, "This must be the leader—he must not escape; he must be taken alive."
translations.idiomatic: More rebels arrived; they pointed and said, "This must be their leader—take him alive, do not let him escape."

sentences.zh: 普叱曰：「死賊奴，我即石都事，何云頭目！」

translations.literal: Pu shouted, "Damned bandit slaves—I am Director Shi—what do you mean by leader!"
translations.idiomatic: Pu shouted, "Damned rebel slaves—I am Director Shi—what leader do you mean!"

sentences.zh: 左脅為賊槍所中，猶手握其槍，斫賊死。

translations.literal: His left flank was struck by a bandit spear; he still grasped the spear and hacked the bandit dead.
translations.idiomatic: A spear struck his left side, yet he still seized the weapon and cut down its bearer.

sentences.zh: 賊眾攢槍以刺普，普與從者皆力戰，俱死之。

translations.literal: Bandits gathered spears to stab Pu; Pu and his followers all fought with all their strength and all died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed spears against him; Pu and his followers fought to the last and all died.

sentences.zh: 盛昭，字克明，歸德人。

translations.literal: Sheng Zhao, style name Keming, was a man of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Zhao, courtesy name Keming, was from Guide.

sentences.zh: 由儒學官累遷淮南行省照磨。

translations.literal: From Confucian school official he was repeatedly promoted to Registrar of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Confucian school official to registrar of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會詔使往高郵，不得達而還，謬稱賊已迎拜，但乞名爵耳。

translations.literal: When an imperial envoy went to Gaoyou but could not reach it and returned, he falsely claimed bandits had already welcomed and bowed, only begging titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy went to Gaoyou but could not reach it, he falsely reported that the rebels had already submitted and only sought titles.

sentences.zh: 行省不虞其欺，乃遣昭入高郵，授所與士誠官。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat did not suspect his deception and sent Zhao into Gaoyou, granting the offices to be given Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat, unsuspecting, sent Zhao into Gaoyou with the offices to grant Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 士誠拒不聽，拘諸舟中。

translations.literal: Shicheng refused to listen and detained him on a boat.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng refused and detained him aboard a boat.

sentences.zh: 昭語所從吏曰：「吾之止此，有死而已。」

translations.literal: Zhao said to the clerks who accompanied him, "My stopping here means only death."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao told the clerks with him, "I can only die here."

sentences.zh: 既而官軍逼高郵，士誠授昭以兵，使出拒官軍，昭叱曰：「吾奉命招諭汝，汝拘留詔使，罪不容斬，又欲吾從汝為賊耶！」

translations.literal: Before long government troops pressed Gaoyou; Shicheng gave Zhao troops and sent him out to resist government troops; Zhao shouted, "I was ordered to summon and instruct you—you detained the imperial envoy, a crime deserving execution, and now you want me to follow you as a bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: When government troops pressed Gaoyou, Shicheng gave Zhao troops and ordered him to resist them. Zhao shouted, "I was sent to summon you to surrender—you detained the imperial envoy, a capital crime—and now you want me to join you as a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 大罵不絕口。

translations.literal: He cursed loudly without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them without cease.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，先剜其臂肉，而後磔之。

translations.literal: Bandits were angry; first they gouged flesh from his arms, then dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels first gouged flesh from his arms, then dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 楊乘，字文載，濱州渤海人。

translations.literal: Yang Cheng, style name Wenzai, was a man of Bohai in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng, courtesy name Wenzai, was from Bohai in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至正初，為介休縣尹，民飢散為盜，乘立法招之，使自新，皆棄兵頓首，願為良民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizheng he was Magistrate of Jiexiu County; the people, hungry, scattered as bandits; Cheng made laws to summon them and let them reform; all cast aside weapons and bowed their heads, wishing to be good subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhizheng he was magistrate of Jiexiu County. When hunger drove people to banditry, Cheng issued laws to summon them to reform; all laid down their arms, bowed, and wished to become law-abiding subjects.

sentences.zh: 其後累官江浙行省左右司員外郎，坐海寇掠漕糧舟免官，寓居松江。

translations.literal: Later he accumulated offices to Vice Director in the Left and Right Offices of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; because sea raiders plundered grain transport boats he was dismissed from office and lodged in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to vice director in the Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat's left and right offices, but was dismissed when sea raiders plundered grain transport boats and took up residence in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 張士誠入平江，其徒郭良弼、董綬言乘於士誠，士誠遣張經招乘，乘曰：「良弼、綬皆名臣，今已失節，顧欲引我，以濟其惡邪！」

translations.literal: When Zhang Shicheng entered Pingjiang, his followers Guo Liangbi and Dong Shou spoke of Cheng to Shicheng; Shicheng sent Zhang Jing to summon Cheng; Cheng said, "Liangbi and Shou are both famed ministers who have now lost their integrity—do they wish to draw me in to aid their wickedness!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng entered Pingjiang, his followers Guo Liangbi and Dong Shou spoke of Cheng to him, and Shicheng sent Zhang Jing to recruit him. Cheng said, "Liangbi and Shou were famed ministers who have lost their integrity—do they now want to drag me in to aid their wickedness!"

sentences.zh: 且讓經平日讀書云何，經俯首不能對。

translations.literal: He also reproached Jing for what his daily reading had been worth; Jing bowed his head and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He also rebuked Jing for what his years of study had amounted to; Jing bowed his head in silence.

sentences.zh: 乘日與客痛飲，竟日不言。

translations.literal: Cheng daily drank heavily with guests and spoke not a word all day.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng drank heavily with his guests day after day and spoke not a word.

sentences.zh: 客問：「盍行乎？」

translations.literal: A guest asked, "Why not leave?"
translations.idiomatic: A guest asked, "Why not flee?"

sentences.zh: 乘曰：「乘以一小吏致身顯官，有死而已，尚何行之有！」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Cheng rose from a minor clerk to a prominent office—there is only death; what is there to flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "I rose from a minor clerk to high office—death is all that remains. What is there to flee!"

sentences.zh: 經促其行愈急，乘乃整衣冠，自經死，年六十四。

translations.literal: Jing urged him to leave ever more urgently; Cheng then arranged cap and robes and hanged himself; he was sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: As Jing pressed him ever more urgently to leave, Cheng put on his cap and robes and hanged himself. He was sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁，字士瞻，其父馬合木，從征襄陽，以勞擢浚州達魯花赤，因家大名。

translations.literal: Nasulading, style name Shizhan—his father Mahemu followed the campaign against Xiangyang, was promoted for merit to Darughachi of Jun Prefecture, and the family settled in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Nasulading, courtesy name Shizhan, was the son of Mahemu, who had campaigned at Xiangyang, was promoted for merit to darughachi of Jun Prefecture, and settled the family in Daming.

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁起身鄉貢進士，補淮東廉訪司書吏。

translations.literal: Nasulading rose from a local tribute jinshi and was enrolled as a clerk in the Huaidong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Nasulading entered office as a local tribute jinshi and became a clerk in the Huaidong surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，補兩浙鹽運司掾，復辟掾淮東宣慰司。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was enrolled as a clerk in the Liang-Zhe Salt Transport Office, then recalled as clerk of the Huaidong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death and the mourning period, he became a clerk in the Liang-Zhe salt transport office, then was recalled to the Huaidong pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 至正十年，賊發真州，納速剌丁以民兵往襲之，獲賊四十二人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhizheng bandits rose in Zhen Prefecture; Nasulading led militia in a raid and captured forty-two bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhizheng rebels broke out in Zhen Prefecture; Nasulading led militia in a raid and captured forty-two of them.

sentences.zh: 已而泰州賊大起，鎮南王府宣慰司請參議軍事，納速剌丁建議築四城，立外寨，揵堤穿河，募兵與賊抗。

translations.literal: Before long bandits rose greatly in Taizhou; the Prince of Zhennan's Pacification Commission requested him to discuss military affairs; Nasulading proposed building four cities, establishing outer stockades, driving dikes and cutting canals, and recruiting troops to resist bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels rose in force in Taizhou; the Prince of Zhennan's pacification commission asked him to advise on military affairs. Nasulading proposed building four fortified towns, outer stockades, dikes and canals, and recruiting troops to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 行省檄其提戰艦六十、海舟十四，上下巡捕，以固江面。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat ordered him to lead sixty war junks and fourteen sea boats to patrol up and down and secure the river surface.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat ordered him to lead sixty war junks and fourteen sea boats on patrol to secure the river.

sentences.zh: 且護蒙古軍五百往江寧，道遇賊，斬擊二百餘級，生獲十八人，遂抵龍潭而還。

translations.literal: He also escorted five hundred Mongol troops to Jiangning; on the road they met bandits, beheaded more than two hundred, captured eighteen alive, then reached Longtan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also escorted five hundred Mongol troops to Jiangning; on the way they met rebels, killed more than two hundred, took eighteen prisoners, reached Longtan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出邏江上，賊突至，馳船來鬥，納速剌丁手射死三十賊，奪其放火小船二百，賊因遁走。

translations.literal: Before long he went out to patrol the river; bandits suddenly arrived and raced boats to fight; Nasulading personally shot thirty bandits dead, seized two hundred of their fire-setting small boats, and bandits therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was patrolling the river when rebels suddenly attacked by boat; Nasulading personally shot thirty dead, seized two hundred of their fire ships, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 俄复據龍潭口，又擊走之，追斬三百餘級。

translations.literal: Before long they again held Longtan mouth; he again struck and drove them off, pursuing and beheading more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: They soon reoccupied Longtan mouth; he drove them off again and pursued, killing more than three hundred.

sentences.zh: 其子寶童擒首賊陳亞虎等及其號旗。

translations.literal: His son Baotong captured the chief bandit Chen Yahu and others along with their signal banners.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baotong captured the rebel chief Chen Yahu and others along with their banners.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賞賚良渥，且召納速剌丁還真州。

translations.literal: When victory was reported rewards were generous, and Nasulading was summoned back to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported he received generous rewards and was summoned back to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而賊犯蕪湖，南行台檄使來援，乃以兵赴。

translations.literal: But bandits invaded Wuhu; the Southern Branch Secretariat dispatched orders for aid, and he went with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels invaded Wuhu the southern censorate platform ordered aid, and he marched to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 及至，賊船已薄岸，遂三分戰艦，縱擊之，賊奔潰，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: When he arrived rebel boats had already pressed the shore; he then divided war junks into three parts and struck freely; bandits fled in defeat and very many were captured or beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived rebel boats were already at the shore; he divided his fleet into three columns and attacked; the rebels fled in defeat and many were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 賊不得渡江者，多納速剌丁之功也，因留守蕪湖江口。

translations.literal: That bandits could not cross the river was largely Nasulading's achievement; he therefore remained to guard the mouth of Wuhu on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: That the rebels could not cross the Yangzi was largely due to Nasulading; he remained to guard the mouth of Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 泰州李二起，行省移之捍高郵得勝湖。

translations.literal: Li Er rose in Taizhou; the Branch Secretariat transferred him to defend Desheng Lake at Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Er rebelled in Taizhou, the branch secretariat transferred him to defend Desheng Lake at Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 賊船七十餘柁，乘風而來，即前擊之，焚其二十餘船，賊潰去。

translations.literal: More than seventy rebel boat masts came riding the wind; he immediately advanced and struck them, burned more than twenty of their boats, and bandits fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy rebel boats came on the wind; he attacked at once, burned more than twenty, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 李二失援，遂降。

translations.literal: Li Er lost support and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Er, cut off from support, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其黨張士誠殺李二，復為亂，戕參政趙璉，入據興化，而水陸襲高郵，屯兵東門。

translations.literal: His follower Zhang Shicheng killed Li Er, rebelled again, killed Vice Administrator Zhao Lian, entered and held Xinghua, and by land and water attacked Gaoyou, encamping troops at the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Zhang Shicheng killed Li Er, rebelled again, killed Vice Administrator Zhao Lian, seized Xinghua, and attacked Gaoyou by land and water, encamping at the east gate.

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁以舟師會諸軍討之。

translations.literal: Nasulading with naval forces joined the various armies to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Nasulading joined the campaign with his fleet.

sentences.zh: 距三垛鎮，賊眾猝至，納速剌丁麾兵挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Near Sanduo Town rebel masses suddenly arrived; Nasulading commanded troops to blunt their vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Near Sanduo Town a large rebel force suddenly arrived; Nasulading commanded his troops to blunt their attack.

sentences.zh: 後賊鼓譟而前，乃發火筒火鏃射之，死者蔽流而下。

translations.literal: Later bandits advanced with drums and clamor; he then fired fire-tubes and fire-arrows at them; the dead covered the current flowing downstream.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels advanced again with drums and shouts, he fired fire-tubes and fire-arrows; corpses choked the current downstream.

sentences.zh: 賊繚船於背，盡力來攻，而阿速衛軍及真、滁萬戶府等官，見賊勢熾，皆遁走。

translations.literal: Bandits moored boats behind and attacked with all their strength; but Asud Guard troops and officials of the Zhen and Chu Ten-Thousand-Household Offices, seeing bandit power fierce, all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels moored boats behind and attacked with all their strength; but the Asud Guard and officials of the Zhen and Chu ten-thousand-household offices, seeing the rebel force was overwhelming, all fled.

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁顧必死，謂其三子寶童、海魯丁、西山驢曰：「汝輩可脫走。」

translations.literal: Nasulading saw he must die and said to his three sons Baotong, Hailuding, and Xishanlu, "You may escape."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he must die, Nasulading told his three sons Baotong, Hailuding, and Xishanlu, "You should escape."

sentences.zh: 寶童等不肯去，遂皆死之。

translations.literal: Baotong and the others would not leave and all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Baotong and his brothers would not leave, and all died with him.

sentences.zh: 省憲為賻其家。

translations.literal: The provincial surveillance officials provided condolence payment for his family.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities provided condolence payments for his family.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈納速剌丁淮西元帥府經歷。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Nasulading was posthumously granted Administrator of the Huaixi Grand Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, the court posthumously appointed Nasulading administrator of the Huaixi grand marshal's office.
